relations.label: If the option is now openly priced and the old restraint does not return when the fee is dropped, a seller who wants the door shut again must build a new fee, and every new fee begins as a threat the seller hopes never to collect, one register lower each turn, as the library that abolishes fines and instead bills replacement cost after thirty days; the loop has one exit, which is to give up the door for a price that goes to sleep, as the video store's abolished late fees gave way to a subscription with no door at all.

relations.from: Rack rate: a list price nobody pays, kept so that every real price can be a discount from it, granted selectively and felt as a favor, and so that a third party can be billed against it, as the hotel's posted rate and the hospital chargemaster that only the uninsured and the insurer's formula ever meet; the carrier is the discount, the price is for the very good on sale yet clears nothing for anyone, and removing it does not lower prices but removes the seller's power to give.
relations.to: Price for the stranger's eyes: a price set for a reader who is not party to the trade, because each recorded price is evidence in the next one, as the gallery bids on its own artist at auction so the record will not print a low number, the recorded house sale sets the neighbor's assessment, and the transfer price between two subsidiaries is addressed to the tax authority alone; the carrier is the public record, and the clearing story cannot explain a seller who refuses cash to protect a number. Exchange-ontologies lists Precedent as a good that can be traded; this is the mechanism by which an ordinary price takes a second job as precedent whether the parties want it or not.
relations.label: If the only recorded price is the rack rate, the record testifies to a number nobody paid, so the stranger who reads it, the insurer's formula, the assessor, the next patient, is billed against fiction; a rack rate can recruit a public record and then poison it.

relations.from: Go-away price: a bid padded past any number the seller expects to win, so an unwanted counterparty is refused without a refusal and the door stays open for the next job, as the roofer who dislikes the client quotes triple and the fisherman names a price for the tourist's charter he hopes never to run; unlike the rope, which thins a population in advance, this refuses one counterparty after seeing them, and it forks on acceptance, since a go-away price that is paid becomes an obligation at a number that was meant as compensation for reluctance.
relations.to: Velvet rope: a price set high enough that the crowd it admits becomes the product for everyone in it, as the nine-dollar coffee keeps the coworking floor quiet by pricing out anyone who came to sit for an afternoon, and the private bank's minimum balance sells its other clients' company; the carrier is the buyer population, the seller wants fewer buyers of a particular sort, and the quantity a clearing price would sell is the failure rather than the goal.
relations.label: If go-away prices are accepted often enough that the seller stops padding them and starts publishing them, one-by-one refusals become a rope: the number that refused a client now selects a clientele, and the seller learns which kind of buyer they had been refusing only from who walks in.

exploration.first_question: What does a price accomplish other than clearing a market, through what carrier, and what does the clearing story miss about it, so that optimizing the number as if it were only a price breaks the other job?
exploration.changed_question: Which prices do their work by not being paid, never charged, refunded, listed but discounted away, or attached to a good nobody buys, and what happens when a price built to stay unpaid starts to be collected? Breath one assumed a price is something a buyer pays and asked what the payment does; sharpening the cancellation fee, which had surfaced under Six-minute increment as a meter that teaches by never being charged, against the restaurant deposit produced a family of prices whose success is a zero on the till.

priorities.item: Fee that holds the door: a price the seller hopes never to collect, as the cancellation fee, the late fee, and the liquidated-damages clause, which work by being believed and stop working when they are paid often, since a fee collected often enough to be optimized as revenue becomes a rack rate for lateness and the door it held swings open; the carrier is the threat, nothing changes hands on the good path where the deposit changes hands twice, and the clearing story sees a fee that is never paid as a price with no demand.
priorities.why: It is the one item whose failure mode is a bookkeeping event, so it can be caught in any company's own ledger; it also looks like the general form of every price that is a threat, and the loop through the invoice is the map's sharpest claim about what breaks under optimization.
priorities.next_question: Take one product with a cancellation or late fee, compute the fee's share of revenue over the last eight quarters, and on a random half of new customers raise the fee by a fifth for one quarter: if lateness falls and revenue is flat the fee is still a door, and if revenue rises with lateness flat it has already become a rack rate for lateness and the door is gone.

priorities.item: Price for the stranger's eyes: a price set for a reader who is not party to the trade, because each recorded price is evidence in the next one, as the gallery bids on its own artist at auction so the record will not print a low number, the recorded house sale sets the neighbor's assessment, and the transfer price between two subsidiaries is addressed to the tax authority alone; the carrier is the public record, and the clearing story cannot explain a seller who refuses cash to protect a number. Exchange-ontologies lists Precedent as a good that can be traded; this is the mechanism by which an ordinary price takes a second job as precedent whether the parties want it or not.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that it is common outside art and property, high generative promise: if an ordinary price acquires a second job as precedent, then sellers should sometimes refuse a good offer to protect a number, and the size of that refusal is a measurable price the clearing story says cannot exist.
priorities.next_question: In one market with public price records (auction lots, recorded house sales) and one without (private dealer sales, off-market houses), count sales withdrawn or bought in near the reserve over a year; if the public market withdraws more at the same demand, the gap is the price sellers pay to keep the stranger's record clean.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing three items (the wrong-payer item's bundled mechanism, the peppercorn's overstated witness, and the decoy's false zero-sales claim), relabeling one edge whose illustration exited the loop it was meant to close, and renaming the seriation axis from how much work the number does to which feature of the price carries it.

neighbors.left: Deposit that comes back: a price returned if the buyer does what they said, so it rations requests by putting money at risk rather than by collecting it, as the restaurant deposit refunded on arrival, earnest money on a house, and bail; the carrier is escrow, the net price is zero for everyone who keeps their word, and the clearing story cannot see a price that changes hands twice and ends where it began. It also earns the seller float, which is the one number in it a spreadsheet will find.
neighbors.right: Fee that holds the door: a price the seller hopes never to collect, as the cancellation fee, the late fee, and the liquidated-damages clause, which work by being believed and stop working when they are paid often, since a fee collected often enough to be optimized as revenue becomes a rack rate for lateness and the door it held swings open; the carrier is the threat, nothing changes hands on the good path where the deposit changes hands twice, and the clearing story sees a fee that is never paid as a price with no demand.
neighbors.separating_case: A wedding venue that takes a five-thousand-dollar deposit refunded on the day, against one that writes a five-thousand-dollar cancellation fee: on the good path the deposit changes hands twice and the fee never once; the deposit rations intent from the moment it is paid and earns the venue float whether or not the couple shows, while the fee rations nothing until it is believed and earns nothing until someone cancels. The case that separates them is the venue's own wish: it wants the deposit back in the couple's hands, and it wants the fee never to leave theirs.

checks.boundary_case: A discount behind an identity fence (the student price checked at the door, the drug priced by country with reimport banned) is out: it looks as if the price is doing extra work, but each segment clears at its own number and the wall, not the price, is the instrument. Rack rate is in on exactly that contrast, since nobody in any segment pays it.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Fee that holds the door → Invoice that ends the favor → Fee that holds the door, where a fee collected often enough to be optimized becomes the open price of an option, the old restraint does not return when the fee is dropped, and the seller must build a new threat one register lower; the loop has one exit, named on the edge, which is to give up the door for a price that goes to sleep, so the loop is also a fork between a lower door and a sleeping price. It shows an incompatibility between seriation neighbors, Velvet rope → Price as testimony, where a price that succeeds as testimony recruits the crowd the rope existed to thin. It shows two passages between levels, Six-minute increment → Tier that makes the kind, where a meter's instruction to individual buyers becomes a category in the market's vocabulary, and Go-away price → Velvet rope, where one-by-one refusals published become a screen on a class. And it shows two dependencies, Price that names the wrong payer → Price that goes to sleep, where a price with no payer at the user has no bill to wake, and Rack rate → Price for the stranger's eyes, where an unpaid list price poisons the record that third parties read.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not a self-read: the critic found no item restating a grown list and no strange member softened into advice; the three repairs (wrong payer, peppercorn, decoy) each kept the original strange mechanism and sharpened its discriminator after showing the original text failed on its own cases, the edge relabel kept the loop and named its exit, and the axis rename moved no station; the repairer preserved nothing against the critic because no repair replaced a strange mechanism with a respectable different one.

name: market-births
of: A precondition, whether a unit, a rule, a place, a record, a party, a date, or a property of the good itself, that must exist before a thing can be priced and traded at all, named with a wanted market whose absence it explains, and sorted by whether the market makes it for itself, builds it on outside credit, converts it from a hostile form already present, must have it brought from outside, or cannot have it at all.
items: Cut to a lot: nothing can carry a price until a quantity of it has an edge, so the Chicago exchange wrote the contract as five thousand bushels before a bushel traded on it, and radio spectrum was the ether until a license was cut as a band times a territory times a term; not a unit of measure, which both already had, but a unit of sale, the piece that changes hands whole.

Grade that erases the farm: one lot can stand in for another only under a rule that says which lots may replace which, so elevator grades let a Chicago buyer take any No. 2 spring wheat instead of the sack he inspected, while every diamond stays its own lot because the four Cs describe stones without letting one substitute for another, and no diamond futures market has ever held; not the unit, which counts, but the substitution rule, which forgets the farm on purpose, and at its far end a table declaring a tonne of methane to be twenty-eight tonnes of carbon dioxide.

Offers on one wall: a price needs a place where two offers for the same lot can be seen at once by someone able to act on either, so trucking became a spot market when load boards put every posted load on one screen, where before the only wall was inside one broker's head and the broker was the market; adjacent to witness-architectures' Room for strangers, but what is compared here expires, so the wall needs a clock and a stale offer on it is a lie.

Thick before it rots: a seller must find a buyer inside the good's shelf life, so the density of arrivals a market needs is set by decay, and the fish auction fixes one hour before dawn to press a day's scattered landings into one crowd; not a headcount but a ratio, arrivals per shelf life, and the fixed hour is the market manufacturing its own thickness out of sparse traffic.

Comps: a new price can be judged only against remembered ones, so a house with no comparable sales is mortgaged, if at all, on an appraiser's guess, and the first lot of any new kind trades on a price imported from a neighboring market or an appraiser; the memory is the one precondition the market makes for itself, but only from its second trade onward, and a memory seeded with wash trades records prices that were never paid.

Memory pinned to the house: buyers read a posted price as the seller's promise, so a restaurant that charges more on Saturday than on Tuesday is punished as a cheat while an airline selling the same seat under a different fare class is not; the market for the Tuesday table is born when the memory is pinned to the lot rather than the house, by giving the Tuesday table a name of its own as the fixed-price dinner ticket did; not price memory missing but price memory attached to the wrong object.

Queue to hijack: a good rationed by waiting already has a price in the length of the line, so a market can be born on the queue itself, as reservation resellers priced the tables a restaurant gave away free and made the house the unpaid seller of its own scarcity until New York banned the resale in 2024; adjacent to exchange-ontologies' Priority, which names the good, and to clocks-that-are-not-clocks' Queue clock, which reads the line as a wait, this reads the line as a price and names the birth: a market that arrives as a parasite on someone else's rationing and lives only until the host prices the lot, sells the jump itself and keeps the queue as what makes the jump worth paying for, or forbids the trade.

Delivered absence: when the good sold is an event that did not happen, a tonne not emitted or a forest not cut, delivery can be witnessed only against a baseline of what would otherwise have happened, and nobody observed that, so the lot is a subtraction from a story; the market inherits every weakness of the story's author, and no better sensor helps, since what must be sensed is the absence of the thing.

Seller's own witness: a market can be born on a delivery only the seller can attest, as indulgences sold remission in a purgatory no buyer would inspect and offsets are verified by auditors the seller hires; the market's life is then exactly the witness's credit, and because every lot shares one witness, doubt in one attestation is doubt in all of them at once, so such markets do not thin lot by lot as a lemons market does but shrink all together, as the offset market did in 2023 when its forest methodology was doubted; adjacent to witness-architectures' Silence priced as guilt, which is the rule that makes the accused build an honest instrument, this names what a market inherits when no such rule was written.

Finality: a trade exists only from the moment neither party can undo it, so securities settle through a clearinghouse that makes the transfer stick and a house sale stays a relationship until the deed is recorded; there is no market for favors because a favor never settles, and settling one, by naming its price and closing it, would end the relationship it was meant to keep open.

Fence at the lot's edge: a lot can be sold only if third parties can be kept off it, so a fishery has no market in the catch to come until quotas fence the sea, and a spectrum band is a lot only while someone polices interference at its guard band; not the unit but the enforcement of its edge, and the market can draw the line while only a state, a landlord, or a technology can hold it.

Custody out of the maker's hands: the thing must sit somewhere the seller can release it and the buyer can take it without the maker's consent, and a software seat sits in the vendor's activation database, so even after the European court ruled resale of used licenses lawful a used market formed only for the paper licenses that transfer by document and never for the seats the vendor must switch on, because the vendor holds the only shelf; not title, which the buyer may have, but the shelf, and a shelf held by the party who prefers no market is no shelf.

Copy that stays: a sale requires that the seller no longer have the thing, and a dataset sold is a dataset kept, so the buyer pays for a lot the seller still holds and can sell again, and the wanted market for personal data prices at nearly nothing; the cure is to sell access instead of copies, which is a different good with a different custodian.

Lose only by waste: a right that can be lost but not sold is hoarded and used badly, as a Western water right forfeits under beneficial use if left unused yet can rarely be sold across a basin, so the holder's only exit is to spray the water on alfalfa; the way to lose it exists on the wrong door, and the market is born by moving the exit from forfeiture to alienation.

The clock's side: a market stays dormant until some party cannot wait, and which side holds the clock sets which way the price leans, since the fish must sell by noon and the estate by probate, so the buyer takes his time and the price leans down, while the emitter must surrender allowances by April, so the seller takes hers and the price leans up, and family art, where no holder must ever sell and no buyer must ever buy, has no side for its price to lean away from and stays in the attic; not demand or supply, which are wishes, but a date.

Door to say no: a price is a price only if either party could have walked from this trade, to another counterparty or to going without, so the ambulance ride has no market and its price is a levy, and a tow from the roadside is priced by statute for the same reason; monopoly shuts the door to another seller and leaves going without, need shuts going without and leaves the walk to another seller, which is why bread has a market though nobody can go without eating, and only urgency that shuts both doors at once makes a toll booth of the trade, however many sellers exist beyond the next ten minutes.

Money barred: when the community forbids cash as the medium, by a warden or by repugnance, the market is born in whatever substitute the parties can hold, and the substitute's properties then govern it, as prisoners settle in mackerel pouches and once settled in cigarettes that were smoked, so the money supply shrank with use, while kidney donors forbidden to sell trade in chains of paired donations whose marketplace is a matching algorithm rather than a price; not a settlement failure but a bar on the medium, which a market can route around at a cost the substitute sets: a smoked money loses its supply, and a matching algorithm keeps the trade but loses the price.

Price-proof good: some goods are changed by being paid for, so the priced thing is a different thing, and an apology bought is not an apology, a bought review is an advertisement, a bought vote no longer says what the voter thinks; there is no market for apologies not because a unit, a witness, or a medium is missing but because the good carries its own motive, and this is, as far as this map can see, the one precondition nothing built can supply.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: grain grades, load boards, fish auctions, activation databases, water forfeiture, mackerel pouches, kidney chains, indulgences; drawn from commodities, freight, software, restaurants, carbon, medicine, prisons, and church history.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism. The sorting of preconditions into self-made, credit-built, converted, and imported is the author's interpretation; Price-proof good's claim that payment changes the good is analytical rather than measured; no item is speculative or invented-world.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a checklist or a partition; a real market needs most of these at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind of precondition.

The seriation is an itinerary of how much of each precondition the market can make for itself, not a ranking of importance, cost, or the order in which a founder should build; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (Chicago elevator grades, the UsedSoft ruling, offset registries, the 2024 New York reservation law, Western beneficial-use doctrine, Radford's camp and the mackerel economy, indulgences) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the full histories.
Whether a market should exist is outside the list; Money barred and Price-proof good describe what a bar does to a market's shape, not whether the bar is right.
Market deaths and manipulations (cornering, wash trading, delisting) are outside except where they appear as a birth's failure mode, as in Comps and Seller's own witness.

seriation.axis: How much of the precondition the market can make for itself: from lots, grades, walls, hours, and memory that the exchange writes into being, through preconditions already present in a hostile form that the market must convert (a menu price, a queue), to preconditions the market can build only on outside credit (a baseline, a witness, a settlement, a fence someone else must police), to preconditions brought whole from outside (a shelf, a loss, a date, a door), and finally the good's own nature, which nothing built can alter.
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of difficulty or a construction order. Cut to a lot opens it because the exchange can write the lot with a pen; Price-proof good closes it because no pen reaches the good. Comps sits at the first hinge, the last self-made precondition, and it teaches that even the market's own memory needs one imported price to start. The consequential adjacency is Money barred → Price-proof good: both look like repugnance from outside, but a bar on the medium can be routed around, as kidney chains and mackerel show, while a bar inside the good cannot, since an apology traded in kind is still not an apology; the walk ends exactly where conversion stops working. The middle pair Memory pinned to the house → Queue to hijack holds the second breath's discovery, that some markets are born by converting a precondition that is present in the wrong form rather than by supplying one that is absent. Lose only by waste is counted among the births by conversion in the ledger yet walks here with the imports, after Copy that stays, because the converter must be a legislature rather than any market participant: it is a conversion the market cannot perform for itself, which is exactly what the imported band means.

relations.label: If cash is barred, the market can be rebuilt in kind and still trade the same good, as a kidney given for a kidney is still a kidney; but if the good is price-proof no medium rescues it, since an apology exchanged for an apology is still not an apology, so the bar sits on the medium in one case and inside the good in the other, and only the first can be routed around.

exploration.first_question: What must exist before a thing can be priced and traded at all: which unit, custody, witness, standard, settlement, refusal, place, title, party, or memory is missing when a market everyone says they want does not exist?
exploration.changed_question: Which of these the market can manufacture for itself, which it can build only on outside credit, and which are already present in a form that forbids the market, so that the birth is a conversion (renaming the lot, moving the exit from forfeiture to sale, routing around a barred medium) rather than a construction. The first breath assumed each precondition was either present or absent; the restaurant's Tuesday night and the Western water right both had their precondition present and attached to the wrong object, and the kidney chain had a market with every precondition except the medium.
exploration.new_member: Memory pinned to the house: buyers read a posted price as the seller's promise, so a restaurant that charges more on Saturday than on Tuesday is punished as a cheat while an airline selling the same seat under a different fare class is not; the market for the Tuesday table is born when the memory is pinned to the lot rather than the house, by giving the Tuesday table a name of its own as the fixed-price dinner ticket did; not price memory missing but price memory attached to the wrong object.

priorities.item: The clock's side: a market stays dormant until some party cannot wait, and which side holds the clock sets which way the price leans, since the fish must sell by noon and the estate by probate, so the buyer takes his time and the price leans down, while the emitter must surrender allowances by April, so the seller takes hers and the price leans up, and family art, where no holder must ever sell and no buyer must ever buy, has no side for its price to lean away from and stays in the attic; not demand or supply, which are wishes, but a date.
priorities.why: It is a date rather than an institution, so it can be inspected in any dormant market in an afternoon, and it predicts the direction of the first prices, which no other item does.
priorities.next_question: Take one dormant market everyone wants (used software seats, or water in one basin) and for each of its ten largest holders write the date, if any, by which they must sell or buy; if the column is empty, add one date on paper (a lease expiry, a compliance deadline, a use-it-or-sell-it rule) and count how many holders it would bring to the wall, and on which side.

priorities.item: Price-proof good: some goods are changed by being paid for, so the priced thing is a different thing, and an apology bought is not an apology, a bought review is an advertisement, a bought vote no longer says what the voter thinks; there is no market for apologies not because a unit, a witness, or a medium is missing but because the good carries its own motive, and this is, as far as this map can see, the one precondition nothing built can supply.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that its boundary is fixed, high generative promise: if the good is changed by who receives the money rather than by money's presence, then a class of markets everyone calls impossible is merely unbuilt.
priorities.next_question: Design an apology bond in which the apologizer posts money that is forfeited to a third party if the apology is later judged insincere, and run it on a small forum against unbonded apologies; if bonded apologies read as more sincere, the price-proof boundary runs through who receives the payment, not through whether payment exists, and the map's closing item splits.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing eight items (four illustrative cases asserted as history or overloaded as evidence, two discriminators that failed a counterexample, one hidden price-versus-trade distinction in Money barred, one modality clause in Price-proof good) and relabeling four edges, including the Queue-to-hijack fork, which has a third tine the map called impossible.

neighbors.left: Delivered absence: when the good sold is an event that did not happen, a tonne not emitted or a forest not cut, delivery can be witnessed only against a baseline of what would otherwise have happened, and nobody observed that, so the lot is a subtraction from a story; the market inherits every weakness of the story's author, and no better sensor helps, since what must be sensed is the absence of the thing.
neighbors.right: Seller's own witness: a market can be born on a delivery only the seller can attest, as indulgences sold remission in a purgatory no buyer would inspect and offsets are verified by auditors the seller hires; the market's life is then exactly the witness's credit, and because every lot shares one witness, doubt in one attestation is doubt in all of them at once, so such markets do not thin lot by lot as a lemons market does but shrink all together, as the offset market did in 2023 when its forest methodology was doubted; adjacent to witness-architectures' Silence priced as guilt, which is the rule that makes the accused build an honest instrument, this names what a market inherits when no such rule was written.
neighbors.separating_case: A cloud backup vendor's monthly statement that your files are stored: the delivery can be attested only by the seller, so it is the seller's own witness and every customer's confidence dies together if the vendor is caught lying, but the good is a present thing, not an absence, and an outside auditor could verify it by asking for one file back. An offset cannot be verified by asking for the tonne back. Delivered absence is about what kind of thing the good is; Seller's own witness is about who is paid to see it, and a present good can suffer the second without the first.

checks.boundary_case: Trust between the parties is out: it is not a thing that must be built but a summary of several that are, and every case where a market is said to lack trust decomposes into a missing witness, a missing finality, or custody held by the wrong party. Willing counterparties are out for the opposite reason: wanting the market is the premise of every case here, not a precondition of trade.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals at Queue to hijack → Memory pinned to the house: once a parasite market has shown the host its price, the host absorbs the market by naming the lot, sells the jump itself and keeps the queue as what gives the jump its price, or kills the market by decree; only the first tine leads to the Tuesday table, and the second, on which the queue and a market survive together, is the path the sequence hides. It shows a loop at Offers on one wall → Comps, where the wall feeds the memory that judges the next price, opened only by a first price imported from outside. It shows a dependency at Delivered absence → Seller's own witness, since a baseline nobody observed must be authored, by the seller, the seller's hire, or a standard-setter, and every author leaves one shared story whose doubt shrinks every lot at once. It shows an incompatibility at the limit at The clock's side → Door to say no, where the same variable, how long a party can wait, supplies the market's buyer at one value and shuts both doors of refusal, going without and the walk to another seller, at another, so the ambulance is the allowance auction with the clock tightened. And it shows a passage between levels at Money barred → Price-proof good, where a bar that could be routed around at the level of the medium becomes, one level down inside the good, a bar nothing can route around.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not a self-read: the critic tried to collapse Thick before it rots into The clock's side and Cut to a lot into Fence at the lot's edge and could not, ruled scarcity a summary rather than a member, and found the strange members (a market born as a parasite on a queue, money that shrinks because it is smoked, a good destroyed by its own price, a right lost only by wasting it) kept as mechanisms; the eight repairs corrected cases asserted as history, two discriminators that failed a counterexample, and one flat universal, without softening any mechanism into advice.

name: deal-deaths
of: A mechanism by which a deal both principals wanted at a price both would have accepted fails to close without the world, the calendar, or either party's valuation changing from outside, named by the carrier that kills it, an arrangement that existed before the talks, a structure inside one party, the talks themselves, or the act of closing, and by what an outsider misreads the death as.
items: No line to put it on: both principals want the trade but the paying side's books have no category the payment can post to, as when a company wants to pay an open-source maintainer and has a vendor-onboarding path but no purchase that fits it, a hospital wants a device that is neither capital equipment nor a consumable, or the early Franciscans wanted bequests their rule forbade them to own until a fictive owner was invented; an outsider reads low priority, but the want is intact and the transaction has no name in the one place it must be written.

Missing witness: the closing instrument requires an attestation from a third party that nobody can produce, as a business sale that needs audited accounts from a seller who never kept auditable books, or a grain forward that needs a warehouse certificate the elevator cannot issue; not distrust between the principals, who may both believe the fact, but a form that will not accept belief, and where witness-architectures' missing witness kills the fact, this one leaves the fact standing and kills the trade.

Signer with no upside: a required consent belongs to someone who gains nothing by giving it and is blamed if it goes wrong, as a landlord asked to consent to a lease assignment, a bonding surety asked to approve a change order, or a co-heir; silence is that signer's best move and it runs on no clock unless a deemed-consent rule has been written onto that one signature, the cure that names the killer, so an outsider reads bureaucratic delay while the deal dies of an asymmetry at one signature the principals cannot buy past without making the signer a party.

Third chair's clause: a term both principals would accept is forbidden or multiplied by a clause in one party's contract with someone not in the room, as a most-favoured-nation clause that propagates a grocer's discount to every other grocer, a reinsurance treaty that excludes the risk the underwriter wants to write, or a lender covenant that forbids the waiver; an outsider reads stubbornness over a small term, but the negotiator is refusing the portfolio the term would sign, and the killer sits in a chair outside the room.

Champion's single-tender want: an organization's want for a deal is held entirely in one sponsor's political capital, so when that person leaves or is reassigned the deal has no holder though the business case is untouched; an outsider reads a change of strategy, but nothing about the deal changed except who could be blamed for it, and nobody arriving cold spends their own capital on a stranger's deal.

Ratifier's other deal: the negotiator was not the principal, and the body that must ratify, a membership, a board, a spouse, a head office, had been wanting a different deal all along, so the term sheet arrives as a stranger's bargain, as when a membership votes down the tentative agreement its own leadership signed; an outsider reads bait-and-switch, but both negotiator and ratifier still want a deal, only not the same one, and the mandate was narrower than either side of the table believed.

No sentence to say it with: a principal wants the terms but has no form of words in which its own audience can hear them without hearing defeat, as a union offered under a new name the term it struck against, or a ministry offered what it had called unacceptable; an outsider reads pride, but the deal lacks an announcement rather than a price, and where impasse-inventions' face-saving fiction is the chip, this is the death when no fiction can be minted.

Report that must be acted on: a defect the seller always knew and the buyer would have priced becomes, once written in a diligence report, a record that the buyer's lender, insurer, or board is obliged to act on, as contamination under a site the seller has run for thirty years; not a hidden fact surfacing, since the fact was tacitly priced by both, but a tacit fact made a record, and an outsider reads concealment where there was only silence.

Concession-made option: a concession reveals a need or a divisibility that creates an alternative that did not exist when talks began, as a buyer whose demand for exclusivity teaches the seller that a rival would bid, or a seller whose willingness to carve out one asset teaches the buyer that the asset alone can be had elsewhere; not a hidden alternative surfacing but one manufactured by the talks, and an outsider reads the other side shopping the deal.

Paid in the tasting: the negotiation delivers enough of the good that the deal is no longer needed, as an acquisition for a team's know-how whose diligence sessions transfer enough of it to build without them, or a partnership whose joint planning teaches each firm what the other knew; distinct from the concession-made option because no third party appears and the buyer's alternative is now its own hands, and an outsider reads a buyer who used the seller.

Parties changed by talking: a long negotiation replaces the party the deal was fitted to, without transferring anything, as a founder who spends a year explaining the company to a buyer and discovers in the telling that she does not want to leave it, or a target's engineers who learn what the acquirer is like and resign before signing; not cold feet, since the parties who began still want the deal they began, and those parties no longer exist, and not Paid in the tasting, since nothing was consumed and the death is measured by who now sits in the chair rather than by what either side can do alone.

Price found too precisely: a deal closes inside a zone of mutual ignorance about where in the zone it sits, and when a leak or a disclosed second bid shows one side exactly how much it left on the table, that side can no longer sign in front of its own ratifier though the price still beats its alternative; not a change in value or in reservation but in the legibility of the split, and an outsider reads greed.

Retrade turns price into character: a price cut delivered after the other bidders have been dismissed under exclusivity converts a price question into a question about the counterparty's honesty, which the seller cannot price and will not pay, though the retraded number still clears its reservation; an outsider reads the seller as irrational, but the seller has noticed that it is being asked to sign with someone whose next retrade it cannot see.

Cost of the last mile: closing costs accrue with every week the deal stays open, counsel, held attention, deferred decisions, an expiring rate lock, until the remaining cost to close exceeds the remaining surplus for one side though the surplus never shrank; an outsider reads lost interest, but the deal died on a curve, and by analogy a honeybee swarm that cannot reach quorum on a nest site before its stores run down dies on the same curve.

Self-moving denominator: the price is denominated in something the deal's own announcement moves, as a stock-for-stock merger whose announcement drops the acquirer's shares through the collar, a business whose customers leave on hearing it is for sale, or a team whose acquisition brings every member an outside offer, so the deal signed is not the deal that reaches closing; not the market moving but the deal moving its own unit, and an outsider reads bad luck in timing.

Ghost closing: the deal is lived before it is signed, shipments on a handshake, a venture run on a memorandum, so signing loses its urgency, and when the first dispute arrives there is nothing to enforce and the dispute becomes the negotiation; speculative in its strong form, that the first dispute either signs the paper or kills the deal and never neither, and an outsider reads a broken contract where there was never one.

Paper as insult: the parties have agreed and often already performed, and the request for a signed document is read as a withdrawal of trust, as when a prenuptial agreement ends the engagement it was meant to protect or a cofounder's request for a vesting schedule ends the company; both want the substance and the form kills it, an outsider reads that they never really agreed, and a standard form authored by no one is the one paper that carries no accusation.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: budget lines, warehouse certificates, landlord consents, most-favoured-nation clauses, ratification votes, diligence reports, exclusivity retrades, rate locks, stock collars, handshakes, prenuptial agreements; drawn from acquisitions, leasing, insurance, grocery supply, grain, software, open source, labour bargaining, construction bonding, one monastic order, and one beehive.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; Ghost closing's strong form is speculative and says so, the swarm in Cost of the last mile is an analogy, and the seriation's claim that visibility from inside tracks the itinerary is an authored interpretation rather than a finding.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real dead deal usually has several of these carriers at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

'Both principals wanted' is idealized: want is taken at the reservation price as the talks began, so deaths in which a party's valuation changed from outside the deal (the market moved, the subject decayed on the calendar, a real alternative that always existed came into view) are outside, as are deals one side never meant to close; valuations the talks themselves changed (a tasting, a manufactured option, a replaced party) are inside, and the members that still clear both reservations at the moment of death (Price found too precisely, Retrade turns price into character) are the strict sub-case, not the rule.

The seriation is an itinerary of where the killer was made, not a ranking of frequency, cost, or blame; its claim that visibility from inside tracks the itinerary is an authored interpretation, not a measured regularity, and map edges are conditional authored claims.

Illustrative cases (union ratification votes, most-favoured-nation propagation, stock collars, prenuptial agreements, the Franciscan ownership fiction, honeybee quorum) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about specific histories or about bees.

Ghost closing's strong form is speculative and marked so, and the swarm in Cost of the last mile is an analogy, not a claim about bees; nothing here has been checked against a set of actual dead deals.

seriation.axis: Where the killer was made: from deaths that were waiting in the parties' outside arrangements before anyone spoke (a missing category, a missing witness, a consentless signer, a clause in another contract), through deaths made inside one party by the deal's passage through it (a champion, a ratifier, an audience), to deaths the talks themselves manufacture (a record, an option, a tasting, a changed party, a legible split, a retrade, a cost curve), and finally deaths the act of closing manufactures (an announcement, a performance without paper, a signature read as accusation).
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a ranking of frequency, cost, or blame, and not a sequence of stages a dying deal passes through. No line to put it on opens it because the deal is dead before the first word: the killer is a category that was missing before anyone spoke. Paper as insult closes it because nothing is left to kill but the signature itself. Report that must be acted on is the first passage: the diligence report is the talks' first product, and from it on every killer is something the negotiation made. Cost of the last mile → Self-moving denominator is the hinge: the last mile is the last death the talks cause and the announcement is the first the closing causes, and the adjacency teaches that the standard cure for a stalled last mile, announce the deal to force it shut, is the carrier of the next death. The itinerary is also the map's answer to the pointer's question: killers that existed before the talks can be inspected from inside (what line, what witness, who signs, whose clause), killers that are the talks look like progress from inside and are seen from the morgue, and killers made by closing are seen from inside only by someone who has been to the morgue before.

exploration.first_question: By what specific carrier does a deal that both principals still want, at a price both would still accept, fail to close, and which of those carriers can be seen from inside the deal in time to act?
exploration.changed_question: Sorting breath one's deaths by whether they were visible from inside showed that every visible death had a killer that existed before anyone spoke (a category, a witness, a consentless signer, a clause in another contract) and every morgue-only death had the talks themselves as the killer, since from inside the talks look like progress. The question became: which deaths does negotiating manufacture, and does the act of closing, the announcement, the performance, the signature, manufacture deaths of its own?

priorities.why: It is the cheapest death to see from inside and the most often misread as indifference; the probe needs no counterparty's cooperation, only one question to the buyer's finance contact, and a positive result turns category-minting (a subscription instead of a licence, a consumable instead of a device, a fictive owner) into a closing tool rather than a workaround.
priorities.next_question: Take twenty deals stalled past their expected close in one sales pipeline; for each, ask the buyer's finance contact which budget line the first payment would post to and who owns that line; count how many have no answer, then re-ask after the seller reshapes the purchase to fit an existing line; the mechanism predicts that the reshaped ones close and the rest stay stalled for one of the other deaths.

priorities.why: Low plausibility in its strong form (the first dispute either signs the paper or kills the deal, never neither), high generative promise: it says performance before signature does not merely delay paper but sets a trap the first fault springs, which would give operators a reason to sign before the first shipment rather than after the relationship has proven itself, the opposite of the usual advice.
priorities.next_question: Find ten ventures or supply relationships that ran past their intended signing date on a memorandum or a handshake; for each, date the first real dispute and the signature if one ever came; the strong form predicts no case in which the first dispute was followed by neither a signature nor a break within a quarter, and a single counterexample demotes it to the weak form, that ghost closing merely lengthens the window in which Paper as insult can strike.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after restating the item type to the endogeneity criterion the author had actually applied, repairing one item whose first case collapsed into Paid in the tasting, adding the deemed-consent clock to Signer with no upside, and relabeling three edges to remove the fork's no-priced-branch overclaim and to give the incompatibility a concrete antecedent.

neighbors.left: Concession-made option: a concession reveals a need or a divisibility that creates an alternative that did not exist when talks began, as a buyer whose demand for exclusivity teaches the seller that a rival would bid, or a seller whose willingness to carve out one asset teaches the buyer that the asset alone can be had elsewhere; not a hidden alternative surfacing but one manufactured by the talks, and an outsider reads the other side shopping the deal.
neighbors.right: Paid in the tasting: the negotiation delivers enough of the good that the deal is no longer needed, as an acquisition for a team's know-how whose diligence sessions transfer enough of it to build without them, or a partnership whose joint planning teaches each firm what the other knew; distinct from the concession-made option because no third party appears and the buyer's alternative is now its own hands, and an outsider reads a buyer who used the seller.
neighbors.separating_case: An acquirer's engineers sit in the target's design reviews for two months. If they leave knowing how to build the product, the target was tasted, no third party is needed, and the death is measured by what the buyer can now do alone. If instead the target's engineers leave those same reviews knowing what the acquirer pays and carry the number to the acquirer's rival, an option was made and nothing was consumed, and the death is measured by who else is now at the table. Same room, two deaths, and the remedies differ: limit what the buyer sees, or limit what the seller learns about the buyer's need.

checks.boundary_case: A buyer that walks because the market for the asset fell during the talks is out: its valuation changed, so a want died, not a wanted deal. Self-moving denominator is in on exactly that contrast, since there the price moved because the deal was spoken, not because the world moved. A counterparty that never meant to close (cooperative-masks) is out because only one side wanted it, and a deal killed by fraud is out because once the fraud is known the want is gone.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals: from Report that must be acted on, pricing the finding as a headline cut under exclusivity leads to Retrade turns price into character and waiving it leads to Third chair's clause; both branches die, and the only branch that closes hands the finding to an instrument of its own (an escrow, a specific indemnity, a bought policy), which is where impasse-inventions begins. It shows a loop, Retrade turns price into character ↔ Price found too precisely, where each retrade teaches the other side more precision and the loop ends in character rather than in a price. It shows an incompatibility at Missing witness → Paper as insult: the third party's book is unavailable by hypothesis and the party's own representation that substitutes for it is the paper that accuses, so the two deaths together leave exactly one closing instrument, a standard form authored by no one. It shows a passage between levels at Third chair's clause → Ratifier's other deal, where a bilateral price becomes a question about a party's whole book and arrives at the ratifier as a different deal. And it shows a dependency, Ghost closing → Paper as insult, where performance without paper closes the signing window behind itself.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not by the author: the critic restated the type to the endogeneity criterion the author had actually applied, tested the closest neighbors (Paid in the tasting against Parties changed by talking) and a boundary case (financing fell through) against it, and found the strange members (a trade with no category to post to, a signer whose best move is silence, a record that obliges, a number read as character, a document read as accusation, a deal that dies of being announced) intact as mechanisms rather than softened into advice; repairs sharpened cases and antecedents without replacing any mechanism with a more respectable one.

name: deal-flow-attractors
of: A mechanism by which deals bend toward a node without being hunted, named with what the bending costs to maintain, how it decays, and what a second copy of the node does to it, since the attractor may live in the node, in an edge to one counterparty, in a structural position, or in the node's own copies.
items: Tollgate that may not buy: when every deal in a class must pass one desk, the land registry, the port's pilotage association, the exchange's sole clearinghouse, that desk sees every deal first without anyone sending it, and the same compulsion that grants the sight forbids the seat, since a registry that traded on what it registered would lose the rule that makes passage compulsory; it costs the franchise and the conflict rules that keep it, it decays by bypass, and a second registry does not halve the flow but unmakes both, because a title recorded in two books is recorded in neither; not the notary or the title company, which every deal must pass but not this one, since a compulsory class of desks splits on copying like the fast payer and only the singular desk is unmade by its copy; not leverage-discoveries' identity register, which is about what a small edit there moves, since here the question is what the desk may do with what it sees.

Written first look: a right of first refusal, a pre-emption clause, a tenant's option makes the offer compulsory rather than the passage, so the one deal the paper names must be shown to the holder before anyone else; paid for in the earlier deal that wrote it, it expires with the paper and decays sooner by chilling, since other bidders will not spend diligence on a deal the holder can match; it cannot be copied, as two first looks are a queue and not two firsts; not the tollgate, which sees every deal and may take none, since the holder may take the one deal it sees.

Public loser: the underbidder in a famous sale has broadcast, free and credibly, an appetite, a capacity, and a reservation price within one bid of exact, so the next comparable asset is walked to its door; the cost was paid in the lost deal's diligence and continues as anchoring, since every seller now prices to the leaked ceiling, and it decays by clock as the appetite is presumed filled elsewhere; singular by history, since no copy lost that deal; not the habitual bidder, whose continuous signal is discounted precisely because it cost nothing.

Holder of the next lot: the neighbor who owns the adjoining parcel, the firm holding the complementary patent, the pipeline beside the gas field is the highest-value buyer by construction, and sellers who know the assembly premium bring the lot there first; the position costs the carry of the asset that makes it and the premium it invites, since the seller charges the adjacency the holder created, and it decays when the assembly completes or the adjacency stops mattering; the position cannot be copied, though the lot's other neighbors each hold their own; not first-mover-forecloses' acquisition of a bottleneck, which is a move, since this is what holding a position does to what arrives.

Name others need: the anchor tenant, the lead investor, the marquee chef in the food hall receives deals because the rest of the deal cannot close without its participation, so its name is an input the other parties must procure; the name is valuable only while scarce, so the cost is every deal it declines to lend itself to, and it decays by over-lending, since a name on everything certifies nothing; positional, with the count of positions conserved rather than the holder, so a second name splits the flow while each still receives it; not the scarce coin of exchange-ontologies, which the seller wants for itself, since here the name is wanted for third parties.

Room where comparisons happen: the keeper of Lloyd's underwriting floor, the spot market at the port, the saleroom hosts the operation of comparing, and each side comes because the other side is already there, so deals arrive as a byproduct of the comparison; the keeper pays in neutrality, or in dealing that is walled and disclosed, since a room whose keeper is believed to trade against what it sees empties, and the auction house that guarantees lots keeps its floor only by publishing that it does, and in the upkeep of liquidity; it decays when comparison moves elsewhere, and a second room does not split the flow evenly but thins both until one tips, since a comparison of half the market is worth less than half; not Forty jewelers, where the compared parties are themselves the attractor, since here the byproduct goes to the host.

Shelf that draws both sides: the dealer with stock is where buyers go, and sellers, reading the stock as evidence of buyers, bring their goods to the full shop rather than the empty one, so inventory pulls in the direction opposite to what its carrying cost suggests; the loop runs on carry, decays when the stock goes stale, and reverses by itself once the shelf empties, since an empty shelf tells sellers there are no buyers and so stays empty; a second dealer splits both sides and the fuller shelf draws faster; speculative in the inference attributed to sellers, observed in the full shop's unsolicited offers; not the room, which holds nothing, since here the stock is the pivot.

Counterparty of last resort: the pawnbroker, the scrap yard, the salvage buyer, the central bank's window says yes to anything at some price, so flow bends there from two directions, the rejected and the certainty-seeking; it costs the capital to take whatever comes and the adverse selection of receiving what everyone else declined, and it decays on a single no, since always is gone the first time it is not true; on copying the always is conserved and the last is not, as two floors are a market and neither is last; not the whole-carcass buyer, who refuses the half, since this one takes any size at its price.

Named in the no: when the party that declines a deal says whom to try instead, the refusers become an unpaid funnel, and flow bends toward the workout shop, the salvage-title buyer, the contractor who finishes other contractors' jobs without any of them being approached; it costs being known to the refusers and taking the flow they filtered against, and it decays when the refusers start keeping what they used to send, or forget the name; a second such node must be named too, so the split is by the referrer's memory rather than the seller's choice; not the last resort, which the seller knew about before asking anyone, since here the seller learns the destination at the moment of refusal.

The open file: the next deal goes to whoever the counterparty need not onboard, the incumbent bank for the next loan, the vendor already in procurement, the insurer already holding the file, so the attractor lives in the edge between two parties rather than in the node; it costs keeping the file open, compliance and vendor status and a champion who remembers, and it decays when procurement resets or the champion leaves; a copy of the node is not onboarded, so per pair the attractor is not conserved, while across the market the class of open files is; not ghost-leverages' toll at a gate with a free bypass, since the onboarding the file saves is a real cost.

Whole-carcass buyer: the farmer sells the animal to the restaurant that takes all of it, the liquidator takes the whole store, the reinsurer the whole treaty, because the seller's cost of fragmenting the sale routes the whole to whoever can take the whole; it costs a balance sheet sized to the lot and decays as the sheet shrinks; a threshold rather than a rank, so a second buyer able to take the whole leaves the first's flow intact and competes only the price; not the last resort, which takes any size at its price, since this buyer refuses the half.

Retrade-free close: the buyer known never to reprice after the handshake, the publisher who pays on signature, the cash buyer of the house lets sellers accept a lower price for a higher probability, so flow bends toward certainty and the certainty is paid for in the spread; it costs closing the deals one has come to regret, and it decays on one public retrade; conserved on copying, since two reliable closers are both reliable, while the discount each earns is competed away; not paying in speed, which is latency, since a certain closer may be slow.

Paying in speed: the factor, the same-day scrap buyer, the insurer that settles claims in two days draws every seller with a time preference, and the seller pays for the speed in price; it costs a float and the risk of paying before verifying, and it decays the day it slows; a threshold, so conserved on copying; not certainty, since the fast payer may haggle at the gate, and the seller who needs the money by Friday will take that.

Still here next harvest: a deal with a tail, a warranty, a royalty, an earnout, a buyback, prices the counterparty's survival into its terms, so the author chooses the press that keeps the backlist in print and the grower sells to the co-op that will exist next season; it costs visible durability, reserves and age that can be seen, and it decays on any sign of mortality; conserved on copying; not the retrade-free close, whose certainty ends at closing, since here the certainty is for what comes after.

Cheap probe: the dealer who quotes on anything within the hour, the investor who says no in a day and never gossips, is shown everything first because a showing costs the sender nothing, so first refusal arrives by default; it costs answering everything, including junk, fast and silently, and it decays the day a no costs the sender something, a leak, a sulk, a delay; a threshold, so conserved on copying, though the first showing goes to whichever probe is cheapest that morning; not the last resort, since the probe says no more often than anyone.

Confessional: the private bank, the lawyer under privilege, the dealer known to keep the seller's name off the sale draws the deals that cannot be seen, since the seller's cost of being seen routes the deal to the node that cannot tell; it costs never telling, even when telling would win the next deal, and it decays on one leak; conserved on copying; not the room, whose attraction is exactly the visibility this node must lack.

Awake at the hour: the bail bondsman, the tow truck, the night pharmacist takes the deal because at the instant of need the searcher's horizon collapses to whoever answers, and no comparison happens; it costs someone always awake and decays on one unanswered call; a bottleneck in time rather than in structure, and unlike the registry it survives copying, since each caller at three in the morning still meets one node; not leverage-discoveries' bottleneck hour, which is about the power of the scarce input, since here it is the searcher's horizon.

Forty jewelers: Hatton Garden's jewelers, the booksellers' street, the auto mile draw flow to each member because buyers come to compare many at once, so a lone jeweler on a quiet street receives less than one of forty and the attractor is the copies themselves; it costs the rent of the district and being compared, and it decays when comparison moves to a host that lists them all; strengthened by copying up to congestion, so it is the one attractor for which one is the only number that does not work; not the room, whose keeper hosts the comparison, since here each node is one of the compared.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: registries and notaries, rights of first refusal, underbidders, Lloyd's floor, Hatton Garden, pawnbrokers, nose-to-tail carcass sales, bail bondsmen, private banks; drawn from insurance, property, publishing, restaurants, auctions, salvage, freight, and the night trades.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the claims about what copying does are authored reasoning; one item, Shelf that draws both sides, is speculative in the inference it attributes to sellers and says so. Two lines are carried as authored aphorism rather than observed law, at the critic's reading: Counterparty of last resort's 'decays on a single no' means a no within the class the node claimed to take, since pawnbrokers refuse outside it daily; and in the Name others need → Public loser edge, 'the anchor bids only where it will win' is behavioral speculation, since a lead investor seen losing a contested round is not visibly diminished.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real node runs several attractors at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every way flow bends.

The seriation is an itinerary of what a second node does to each attractor, not a ranking of strength, value, or ease; the copy-behavior claims are authored reasoning about mechanisms, not measurements.

The illustrative cases (Lloyd's floor, Hatton Garden, title registries, chilling by rights of first refusal, nose-to-tail carcass sales, night bondsmen) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories.

Adjacent lists are not restated: deal-flow-sources lists where flow comes from, leverage-discoveries lists positions where small inputs have large effects, first-mover-forecloses lists moves; where an item touches one, its discriminator says what it adds. Flow that is hunted, by outreach, advertising, or salience bought with spend, is outside by construction.

Selection effects on the attracted flow are noted only where they are part of an attractor's cost (adverse selection at the last resort, anchoring against the public loser); what volume does to a node's criteria is deal-flow-reflexivities' territory and is left out.

seriation.axis: What a second copy of the node does to the attractor: from annihilated by copying (a second registry unmakes both), through singular by history, positional in a structure, split-and-tipping at the level of the set, copy-inert in the pair (a copy of the incumbent carries nothing and the original is untouched), conserved per threshold while the rent is competed away, to strengthened by copying, where the copies are the attractor.
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of value or a set of stages. Tollgate that may not buy opens it because one is the only number that works for a registry; Forty jewelers closes it because one is the only number that does not work for a row. The hinge is Awake at the hour → Forty jewelers: both are positions in the searcher's horizon, but at three in the morning the horizon holds one node and copying leaves it one, while in the district the horizon holds forty and copying widens it, so the axis turns from horizon-of-one to horizon-of-many in a single step, and the same word, bottleneck, is shown to name two mechanisms with opposite fates under copying, the registry at one end and the night bondsman near the other. Between them the middle stretch, Room where comparisons happen → Shelf that draws both sides, contrasts the host that holds nothing and decays from a rival with the principal that holds everything and decays from within when its own loop reverses. The conserved stretch (Whole-carcass buyer through Confessional) is ordered by where the certainty the seller buys sits in time: the size of the close, the close itself, the payment, the years after. After the critic's repair the opening is clean: the tollgate keeps only singular desks (registry, pilotage association, sole clearinghouse), and the notary and title company, which are compulsory classes that split on copying, are named in its discriminator as members of the conserved stretch rather than of the annihilated end. The critic also named a fifth station the axis statement had left implicit: The open file, between Named in the no and Whole-carcass buyer, is copy-inert rather than split or conserved, which is where the changed question's fourth location, the pair, shows in the itinerary; the order was already right and is unchanged.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanisms does a deal arrive at a node unbidden, what does each mechanism cost to maintain, and how does each decay; and which of them survive when the node is copied?
exploration.changed_question: Where does the attractor live: in the node, in an edge between the node and one counterparty, in a structural position, or in the node's own copies? The first breath put every attractor inside the node as a property or a reputation; sharpening the registry against copying annihilated it, sharpening the incumbent bank against copying showed an attractor the copy cannot carry because it sits in the pair, and the jeweler on the quiet street showed an attractor that is nothing but the copies. Location, not strength, decides what a second node does.
