priorities.item: Written first look: a right of first refusal, a pre-emption clause, a tenant's option makes the offer compulsory rather than the passage, so the one deal the paper names must be shown to the holder before anyone else; paid for in the earlier deal that wrote it, it expires with the paper and decays sooner by chilling, since other bidders will not spend diligence on a deal the holder can match; it cannot be copied, as two first looks are a queue and not two firsts; not the tollgate, which sees every deal and may take none, since the holder may take the one deal it sees.
priorities.why: The chilling loop is a claim about counts that a broker's records already contain, and if it holds, a right of first refusal is a mechanism that empties the field it was written to bend, which changes how an operator prices granting one.
priorities.next_question: Take twenty closed sales in one asset class where a right of first refusal existed and twenty comparable sales without one; count the outside bidders who submitted a diligence-backed offer in each. If the first-look sales average materially fewer, the holder's price was the seller's reservation rather than the market's, and the option was worth more than the party who granted it charged.

priorities.item: Shelf that draws both sides: the dealer with stock is where buyers go, and sellers, reading the stock as evidence of buyers, bring their goods to the full shop rather than the empty one, so inventory pulls in the direction opposite to what its carrying cost suggests; the loop runs on carry, decays when the stock goes stale, and reverses by itself once the shelf empties, since an empty shelf tells sellers there are no buyers and so stays empty; a second dealer splits both sides and the fuller shelf draws faster; speculative in the inference attributed to sellers, observed in the full shop's unsolicited offers; not the room, which holds nothing, since here the stock is the pivot.
priorities.why: The inference attributed to sellers, that a full shelf means buyers, is speculative and cheap to test, and if it holds then inventory is an attractor independent of price, with a reverse loop that explains why an emptying dealer empties faster.
priorities.next_question: Run two identical stalls at one flea market or book fair with the same posted buy prices and signage, one stocked full and one nearly bare, and count unsolicited offers to sell over the day; then drain the full stall through the afternoon and watch whether the offers fall with the stock, which would show the loop running backward.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing the tollgate's illustrative cases, which contradicted the copy fate that anchors the axis, conditioning the room's neutrality claim and the room-confessional fork on the walled dealing auction houses actually practice, relabeling two edges whose consequents overreached their antecedents, and noting that the claimed loop is a one-way passage.

neighbors.left: Retrade-free close: the buyer known never to reprice after the handshake, the publisher who pays on signature, the cash buyer of the house lets sellers accept a lower price for a higher probability, so flow bends toward certainty and the certainty is paid for in the spread; it costs closing the deals one has come to regret, and it decays on one public retrade; conserved on copying, since two reliable closers are both reliable, while the discount each earns is competed away; not paying in speed, which is latency, since a certain closer may be slow.
neighbors.right: Paying in speed: the factor, the same-day scrap buyer, the insurer that settles claims in two days draws every seller with a time preference, and the seller pays for the speed in price; it costs a float and the risk of paying before verifying, and it decays the day it slows; a threshold, so conserved on copying; not certainty, since the fast payer may haggle at the gate, and the seller who needs the money by Friday will take that.
neighbors.separating_case: A municipal buyer that always pays and never reprices, but in ninety days, against a scrap dealer at the gate who pays cash on the spot and haggles when he sees the load: the seller who needs the money to exist goes to the municipality, the seller who needs it by Friday goes to the gate. Certainty and latency are priced separately, and a node can hold either attractor without the other.

checks.boundary_case: Sheer size is out: a big node with no floor, no speed, no name, and no open file receives nothing unbidden, as the conglomerate nobody pitches shows; size is a precondition for several attractors (the whole carcass, the last resort) but bends no flow by itself. Also out by construction is the name that is recalled first because it was advertised: recall bought with spend is the hunt at one remove, not a bending.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals: Room where comparisons happen and Confessional sit ten places apart on the itinerary, but the edge says they are the two branches of one sale's decision, and a node that offers both must wall them. It shows a passage between levels at Forty jewelers → Room where comparisons happen, where the compared become the host's supply, and the same passage repeats one level up when hosts are compared. It shows a one-way passage, not a loop, at Written first look → Counterparty of last resort, where a contract at the annihilated end of the axis chills the field and leaves the seller facing its holder as a floor it cannot test; nothing returns along it (the critic corrected the earlier naming of this as a loop). It shows two incompatibilities, Counterparty of last resort → Shelf that draws both sides (never refuse against curate) and Name others need → Public loser (an anchor cannot afford to be seen losing). And it shows a dependency, Cheap probe → Named in the no, since a refusal that carries a name presupposes a refusal cheap enough to be asked for.
checks.target_preserved: Fable critic (fresh context) judged the target preserved: each item names a distinct reason flow arrives unbidden, a distinct upkeep, decay, and fate under copying, and the strange members (a bottleneck that may not buy, a loss that attracts, a shelf that pulls sellers, a district whose attractor is its rivals, a contract that empties the field it bends) stand as mechanisms after repair; the critic's neighbor test (Cheap probe against Paying in speed: the investor who answers in a day but wires in ninety, against the scrap yard that pays at the gate but will not quote by phone) found them separate, and the critic's boundary test ruled the best price out as the denominator the bending is measured against, not a bending, which reads the of-sentence as bending flow at a price the seller would not otherwise accept.

name: where-margin-hides
of: Mechanisms by which a business's margin lives somewhere other than the sticker price of the thing it appears to sell, each named with its hiding place, the carrier that holds the margin, and the tell that reveals it to an outsider, including what becomes of a hiding place once competitors have found it.
items: Unit mismatch: bought in one unit and sold in another, with the ratio never printed, as the bar buys by the bottle and sells by the glass, the butcher by the carcass and by the cut, and the beekeeper takes honey by the frame and returns sugar by the pail; the carrier is the conversion, and the tell is a menu that names the selling unit but never its size; survives being noticed, since the customer wants the small unit, and the pieces are alike, so no eye is involved.

Breakage: the customer prepays a right and does not exercise it, and the margin is the unexercised part, as gift cards, gym memberships, rebate forms never mailed, and the extended warranty forgotten when the thing breaks, which is a gift card with a scarier name; the carrier is the customer's forecast of their own future, and the tell is a liability that shrinks without cash leaving and reappears as income; survives being known, because notice does not correct the forecast.

Exception fee: the plan is priced at or below cost and the margin is charged when the customer departs from it, as the late fee, the overweight bag, the overdraft, the change fee, the boarding pass printed at the airport instead of at home; the carrier is the customer's own deviation, unpriced at purchase, and the tell is a headline that looks impossible beside a long fee schedule; not popcorn, since the fee is for the departure and not for the normal complement, which is where the checked bag and the prison phone call belong; survives competitors, who copy the schedule, and dies only when the comparison unit is redrawn to include it.

Given-away option: the other side of the trade grants a right it never priced and the business exercises or resells it, as the no-show the airline overbooks against, the bookseller's right to return unsold copies to the publisher, the fair-use clause under the unlimited plan, the right to substitute; the carrier is an asymmetric clause only one side can trigger, and the tell is a contract term the grantor could not have valued alone, since the option is worth something only in aggregate; not breakage, which is the customer's own right left unused.

Loyalty penalty: the first-year price is a bid and the renewal is the business, because the customer's switching cost has become part of the price, as insurers' price walking, the software renewal uplift, the introductory cable rate; the carrier is inertia and nothing consumable, and the tell is new and existing customers paying different prices for the same thing; survives being known, since the customer knows and stays, and was ended in one market only by a rule that priced newcomers and renewers alike.

Popcorn: the item the customer compares is priced near cost and the margin sits in the complement bought where it cannot be compared or brought in, as the cinema, whose ticket goes largely to the studio and whose popcorn is the house's, the restaurant's wine, the stadium's beer, the airport's bottle of water, the checked bag under the seat-only fare; the carrier is the complement inside a watched door, and the tell is a complement at several times its outside price beside a rule against outside food; the captive is the extreme, not a different thing, and the prison phone call is the captive.

Aftermarket: the durable is sold at or below cost and the margin is in the consumable or service the installed base must keep buying, as razor and blade, printer and ink, elevator and maintenance contract, jet engine and power by the hour; the carrier is the installed base as demand that lasts for years, and the tell is a maker who celebrates its installed base and litigates against third-party refills; not popcorn, which is bought on the same visit, since here the complement arrives afterward and the lock is a chip or a contract.

Private mint: the business issues its own unit, sold at face and honored on a menu the issuer writes, as airline miles sold to banks and redeemed for seats that would have flown empty, the coffee chain's stored-value card, the casino chip, the arcade token; the carrier is the right of issue, and the tell is a unit that cannot be turned back into cash; composes float, breakage, and unit mismatch, but the right to write the redemption menu is a margin of its own and survives even if every unit is redeemed.

Financing: the business lends the customer the price and the margin is the interest, so the sticker is a loan's principal and the showroom is a bank, as the dealer's reserve on the car loan, the furniture store that was always a lender, the pay-in-four button; the carrier is the customer's impatience, and the tell is no money down, or a zero-percent offer beside a sticker that will not be discounted for cash; the mirror of float, since here the business waits and is paid for waiting, and not popcorn, since the loan carries a rate the customer could compare and does not.

Float: the business is paid long before it must deliver, and the margin is what the held money earns meanwhile, as an insurer collecting premiums years ahead of claims, or a cemetery selling the plot decades before it digs; the carrier is the interval, and the tell is a business that loses money on every sale it prices and stays solvent; the obligation is owed to the same customer who paid, which separates it from the supplier's clock.

Supplier's clock: the business collects from the customer before it pays the supplier, so growth produces cash instead of consuming it, as a grocer who sells the lettuce in three days and pays the grower in forty-five, or the computer maker paid before the parts are billed; the carrier is the gap between the inventory turn and the supplier's terms, and the tell is cash that rises when sales rise; the obligation is to the supplier, and the supplier, not the customer, carries the margin.

Lot to distribution: bought at the average price of an uneven lot and sold piece by piece at each piece's own price, so the margin is the variance the lot's seller could not or would not price, as the salvage buyer, the pallet of returns, the diamond rough, the lumber grader; the carrier is the grading eye, and the tell is a buyer who refuses to buy piece by piece; not unit mismatch, where pieces are alike and only the ratio hides, since printing the ratio reveals nothing here.

Customer's labor: the served party does work that would otherwise be a wage, as the flat-pack assembled at home, the self-checkout, the buffet, and the bug report; the carrier is the customer's hour priced by the customer at zero, and the tell is a headcount per transaction implausibly low beside a customer who feels free or virtuous; survives notice and copying entirely, so it hides only as long as the customer keeps that price.

Unbilled input: the business depends on an input whose owner sends no bill, as the open-source library under a hosted product, the aquifer under the bottling plant, the public road under the parcel service, the town's name on the label; the carrier is an owner who has not learned to charge, and the tell is a cost of goods that omits something everyone can see the business use; not customer's labor, since the contributor stands outside the trade; ends for every competitor at once when the owner learns, as with a license change or a water district's new tariff.

Exhaust: something the main activity produces incidentally, or leaves idle, is sold to someone else without altering what the customer gets, as the packinghouse's hide and tallow, everything but the squeal, the data center's heat, the church parking lot on weekdays, the sawdust; the carrier is a byproduct or an idle hour with no cost of its own, and the tell is a revenue line whose cost of goods is zero; survives competitors, who have the same exhaust, and its price falls to what the exhaust is worth once they all sell it.

Second payer: the person served is not the person who pays the margin, and the payer shapes what the served receive, as the newspaper whose readers pay for the paper and whose advertisers pay the margin, the slotting fee behind the shelf, the payment for order flow behind the zero commission, the rebate behind the formulary; the carrier is a second contract the customer never sees, and the tell is a visible price below cost; not exhaust, since here the primary act itself is what the other side buys, and the shelf, the feed, and the route bend toward the payer.

Tax shape: the margin lives in the gap between economic and taxable income, chosen by classification rather than by trade, as the sneaker imported with a felt sole so it enters as a slipper, the trust that owes no corporate tax so long as it distributes, the film credit sold to a stranger; the carrier is the state's classifier, and the tell is a business that chooses an inconvenient form, a fuzzy sole or sixteen entities; survives every competitor, who can copy it, and every customer, who never sees it, and dies only when the classifier is rewritten.

Medallion: a hiding place that has survived every competitor gets priced, and the margin leaves the operating business as a payment to whoever held the right first, as the taxi medallion, the liquor license, the water right, farmland whose subsidy is in its price; the carrier is the transferable right, and the tell is an operator who earns nothing on a franchise worth a fortune; not a hiding place the operator can use, but where hiding places go once found and durable, so the margin hides in the past, and the outsider inspecting the operator finds none.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: bars and butchers, cemeteries, packinghouses, cinemas, insurers, grocers, airlines, open-source libraries, taxi medallions, a beehive; mechanisms with tells, not advice.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the two general claims (a hiding place found by every competitor reappears as a sticker loss; a capitalized hiding place recruits the next one) are analytical and marked as such in the limits; no invented worlds.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an accounting taxonomy or a partition; a real business stacks several at once, and an airline loyalty program is a private mint, float, breakage, and a unit mismatch in one line of the accounts.
The seriation is an itinerary by how far the hiding place lies from the customer's attention, not a ranking of profitability, legality, or durability; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (the cemetery plot, the packinghouse, the felt-soled sneaker, price walking, power by the hour, miles sold to banks) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about any firm's accounts.

The claim that a hiding place found by every competitor reappears as a visible loss at the sticker is analytical and observed in some trades (cash-flow underwriting, the free newspaper, the razor below cost); it is not asserted as a law, and how fast competition carries a found margin into the sticker is left open. The further claim that a capitalized hiding place recruits the next one (Medallion → Exception fee) is analytical with no case in hand: the taxi operator's airport surcharge and card fee, offered as the case, are a regulated flat rate and a processor's cost, so the airline programs pledged as collateral in 2020 are the case to check rather than a case held.

Unlawful concealment is outside: short weight past the legal increment, fees that are undisclosed, and tax positions beyond lawful classification; the seller's chosen measurement resolution, which sits at that edge, was left out rather than restated from leverage-discoveries' rounding rule.

seriation.axis: How far the hiding place lies from the customer's attention: from inside the customer's own glass (a ratio they could compute), through the customer's own future conduct (forecast, deviation, inertia), through the shape of the trade over time (the complement, the unit, the interval), to inputs and outputs carried by parties outside the trade, to the state's classifier, and finally to the past, where a found and durable margin has been sold as an asset and left the operator.
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a scale of size or of durability. Unit mismatch opens it because the hiding place is in the customer's own hand and hides only as a ratio nobody prints; Medallion closes it because there the margin is no longer in the business at all. The middle turns twice. After Loyalty penalty the carrier stops being the customer's conduct alone and becomes the shape of the trade over time: the complement (Popcorn, Aftermarket), the unit (Private mint), and the interval, where Financing sits just before Float as the same interval with its sign flipped (the business waits and is paid for waiting; the insurer is paid and waits), and at Float the customer's conduct drops out of the carrier entirely. At Supplier's clock the carrier becomes a margin another party hands over, and Supplier's clock → Lot to distribution → Customer's labor reads as three handed-over margins (the supplier's terms, the supplier's ungraded variance, the customer's unpriced hour) before Unbilled input hands one over from outside the trade; Lot to distribution sits here rather than beside Unit mismatch because its hiding place is the lot seller's unpriced variance, on the supply side and far from the customer's attention, and its discriminator against Unit mismatch holds at either position. The consequential adjacency is Tax shape → Medallion: the tax shape is the most durable hiding place on the route, surviving every competitor and every customer, and durability is exactly what gets a margin priced, so the last hiding place before the medallion is the one most likely to become one; the outsider should read a fat, copyable, invisible margin as a margin about to leave. The two moves (Financing beside Float, Lot to distribution beside Supplier's clock) were the Fable critic's, so that the stated principle, distance from the customer's attention with the carrier's kind as the turning points, is the principle the order follows.

exploration.first_question: Where does a business's margin live when it is not in the sticker price: what is the hiding place, what carries the margin, and what tell reveals it to an outsider?
exploration.changed_question: What becomes of a hiding place once competitors have found it? The first breath wrote each hiding place as if being found ended it, and Float refused: every insurer holds it and knows it, and it shows up not as a vanished margin but as a chronic underwriting loss, the sticker competed below cost by the value of the hidden margin. So a marginless-looking sticker is the signature of a hiding place found by everyone, not of an absent one, and the question became where a found margin goes: into the sticker as a visible loss, and if it survives even that, into an asset price paid to whoever held the right first.
exploration.new_member: Medallion: a hiding place that has survived every competitor gets priced, and the margin leaves the operating business as a payment to whoever held the right first, as the taxi medallion, the liquor license, the water right, farmland whose subsidy is in its price; the carrier is the transferable right, and the tell is an operator who earns nothing on a franchise worth a fortune; not a hiding place the operator can use, but where hiding places go once found and durable, so the margin hides in the past, and the outsider inspecting the operator finds none.

priorities.item: Float: the business is paid long before it must deliver, and the margin is what the held money earns meanwhile, as an insurer collecting premiums years ahead of claims, or a cemetery selling the plot decades before it digs; the carrier is the interval, and the tell is a business that loses money on every sale it prices and stays solvent; the obligation is owed to the same customer who paid, which separates it from the supplier's clock.
priorities.why: The claim that a hiding place found by every competitor reappears as a sticker loss is checkable in one trade with public numbers, and float is the hiding place with the cleanest price for what it hides, the short-term rate.
priorities.next_question: Take twenty years of the property-casualty industry's combined ratio beside the short-term interest rate; if float is a found hiding place, underwriting losses should widen when rates rise and narrow when they fall, lagged by about one renewal cycle; then read free newspapers against advertising rates the same way and see whether the sticker moves by the hidden amount.

priorities.item: Medallion: a hiding place that has survived every competitor gets priced, and the margin leaves the operating business as a payment to whoever held the right first, as the taxi medallion, the liquor license, the water right, farmland whose subsidy is in its price; the carrier is the transferable right, and the tell is an operator who earns nothing on a franchise worth a fortune; not a hiding place the operator can use, but where hiding places go once found and durable, so the margin hides in the past, and the outsider inspecting the operator finds none.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that the loop is general, high generative promise: it says a durable hidden margin is a stage rather than a state, and that the operator who paid for the right is the one who invents the next hiding place.
priorities.next_question: Airline loyalty programs were valued separately and pledged as collateral in 2020; compare each airline's margin outside the program before and after the pledge, and count new fees introduced in the two years after; if the medallion reading holds, the margin has moved from the operator toward the lender and the fee schedule has lengthened in step.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing six items whose cases contradicted their own carrier or grantor (a warranty read as breakage, a captive phone call and a checked bag read as deviations, a supplier-granted option read as customer-granted, a tip read as an hour priced at zero, an idle lot read as a byproduct), relabeling Medallion → Exception fee to drop an undocumented case and state the loop as analytical, and moving Financing beside Float and Lot to distribution beside Supplier's clock so the seriation note is true of the order.

neighbors.left: Breakage: the customer prepays a right and does not exercise it, and the margin is the unexercised part, as gift cards, gym memberships, rebate forms never mailed, and the extended warranty forgotten when the thing breaks, which is a gift card with a scarier name; the carrier is the customer's forecast of their own future, and the tell is a liability that shrinks without cash leaving and reappears as income; survives being known, because notice does not correct the forecast.
neighbors.right: Given-away option: the other side of the trade grants a right it never priced and the business exercises or resells it, as the no-show the airline overbooks against, the bookseller's right to return unsold copies to the publisher, the fair-use clause under the unlimited plan, the right to substitute; the carrier is an asymmetric clause only one side can trigger, and the tell is a contract term the grantor could not have valued alone, since the option is worth something only in aggregate; not breakage, which is the customer's own right left unused.
neighbors.separating_case: One airline no-show. The fare the customer forfeits is breakage: the customer's own right, prepaid and unexercised, and it would survive a ban on overbooking. The seat sold again is a given-away option: a right the contract handed to the airline, worth nothing per ticket and something per flight, and it would survive a rule forcing refunds of no-shows. Two regulations, each killing one and leaving the other, show that the same empty seat carries two different margins with two different carriers.

checks.boundary_case: Growth sold below cost on investors' money (the subsidized ride) is out: it looks marginless because it is marginless, and the margin is a hope located in the future rather than a hiding place in the present trade. It becomes a member on the day the business opens an aftermarket, a loyalty penalty, or a second payer, which is why watching a subsidized business for its first fee schedule is the outsider's tell.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop stated in one label and drawn in two edges: Unbilled input and Tax shape both pass into Medallion, and Medallion → Exception fee returns the route to the customer's side, so a found and durable hiding place capitalizes, leaves the operator marginless, and recruits the next hiding place, and the relabeled edge states analytically that a durable exception fee is itself the next candidate to be rationed and priced, so the route returns toward Medallion; a sequence ending at Medallion would read as a terminus. It shows a fork at Unbilled input, whose margin, once it ends, ends as a tariff (every competitor loses at once) or as a right (the margin capitalizes). And it shows two passages between levels: Popcorn → Aftermarket, where the same complement stretched from a visit to years changes its lock from a door to a chip, and Exhaust → Second payer, where a byproduct's buyer who starts writing the collection spec turns an unaltered service into a bent one, so that a business cannot hold both claims at once.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not by the author: the critic tested the closest pair it chose (Breakage against Exception fee, one gym member mis-forecasting in two directions, separated by two regulators) and a boundary case of its own (the bulk buyer's scale discount) against the declared type, and found the strange members (a margin in the customer's own forecast, a margin in the grading eye, a mint that survives full redemption, a margin that hides in the past) intact as mechanisms rather than softened into advice; the six repairs corrected cases that contradicted their own carrier or grantor without replacing any mechanism with a more respectable one.

name: pricing-unit-metamorphoses
of: Transformations of the unit that is priced that change what the buyer is buying in kind, each naming the old unit, the new unit, and what the new unit obliges: who now carries the measurement burden and the risk, what becomes visible or invisible, what fights it, and what must be true of the thing sold for the new unit to be pricable at all.
items: Assay eats the item: per thing becomes per measured property of the thing, as milk is paid by butterfat and protein rather than the gallon, coal by heat content with penalties for sulfur, and cattle on a carcass grid, so the measurement burden moves to a grader both sides accept and the seller begins breeding, mining, and feeding toward the assay; not a finer price on the same unit, since the buyer now buys the property and the thing that carried it becomes invisible.

Cubed out: the priced unit tends to migrate to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes, and the migration only completes where the constraint is something the buyer can measure too, a cube but not a queue; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price (a tendency observed in freight, not asserted as a law).

Meter in the seller's house: the unit becomes a quantity only the seller can count, as per-seat software becomes per-token inference and the buyer pays a bill they cannot audit for reasoning tokens they are billed for and never receive; the measurement burden leaves the buyer and returns as trust, the cost of verbosity becomes visible while value becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who cannot forecast next month's invoice; not a hidden price, since the rate is published, but a hidden count.

Nearest countable: an outcome nobody can count retreats to the nearest thing a counter both sides accept can inspect, and advances again the day a new counter arrives, as almond growers pay per hive with a frame inspection because pollination cannot be counted, and car insurance moved from per year toward per mile once an odometer plug could be mailed to the buyer; the counter need not be either party, since tokens, impressions, and plays are counted by one side or a fourth and the other side merely accepts; not a proxy chosen for accuracy, since the unit moves toward the newest accepted meter rather than the truest measure (conjectural as a general law, observed in the two cases).

Dead counter: per hour becomes per fixed bid, and the new unit is priced from the old one's records for exactly as long as they are kept, since nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on; a shop that dropped its timesheets when it went to fixed bids is estimating blind within a season, and cannot price a return to hourly estimates either, so the road back closes only behind a move that abandoned a meter, while per-year insurance, which needed no odometer, reopens at will; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.

Rent on the peak: per unit consumed becomes per unit of capacity held ready, as a factory pays a demand charge on its highest kilowatt rather than its kilowatt-hours, a shipper leases a dedicated lane, and a cloud tenant reserves instances that sit idle in its name; the buyer now carries utilization risk and the seller is paid to be idle on the buyer's behalf, the peak becomes visible and the average invisible; not an option that may be oversold, since the reservation must hold at the very moment everyone wants it.

Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.

Thrust by the hour: per machine becomes per hour the machine works, with the seller keeping title and the maintenance, as an airline pays an engine maker per flight hour and a truck fleet pays a tyre maker per kilometre; the seller now carries reliability risk and so gets to design for repair, the meter moves onto the buyer's premises as telemetry, and the buyer's duty cycle becomes visible to the seller while the machine's price disappears; not a lease, since the buyer pays for work done rather than for time held.

Fence around done: per hour becomes per fixed scope, so the price stops measuring effort and starts measuring the completeness of a description, and whoever holds the pen on the description holds the margin, as construction change orders are where a fixed bid is really priced; the seller carries estimation risk, the buyer carries specification risk, effort becomes invisible, and what fights it is scope that grows and corners that get cut; not a coarser time unit, since a day rate still buys time.

Paternity test: per seat becomes per outcome, as software billed per resolved ticket, per hire, or per dollar collected, and an outcome has many parents, so the unit is pricable only when a rule of attribution both sides accept exists before the work; the seller now carries the buyer's competence risk, usage becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who can starve the counter; not a bonus on top of a seat price, since without the attribution rule there is no unit at all.

Paid for the nothing: per treatment becomes per event avoided, as pest control sold as a pest-free season or an energy contractor paid from the bill that never arrived, and a non-event cannot be counted, so the price is pinned to a baseline both sides must fix before the work: last year's count, the untreated strip, the neighbor's field; the fight moves entirely onto the baseline and the work itself becomes invisible; not outcome pricing with a minus sign, since attribution has nothing to attach to and only a control can stand in.

Losers pay the winner: per hour of search becomes per first solution, as a prize, a bounty, or a design competition, so the unit is one success and its price is paid mostly by sellers who never meet the buyer, in failed attempts nobody bills; the buyer carries no risk and the seller population carries all of it, and what becomes invisible is the whole cost of the search; not outcome pricing between two parties, since the buyer buys from a crowd and the crowd's losses are the price.

Head count over hand count: per visit or per repair becomes per head per period with the risk inside, as a clinic on capitation or an extended warranty, so the seller becomes an insurer and the unit is pricable only where heads can be pooled and cannot be chosen after pricing; the seller now wants to select the panel, the panel's risk profile becomes visible and the visit invisible, and which hazard appears depends on who holds the throttle on the event, neglect when the buyer does and stinting when the seller does; not a retainer, which buys availability rather than a person's risk.

Audit is the unit: per unit sold becomes per share of the buyer's take, as percentage rent in a mall, a royalty, a sharecropper's third, or a bookseller's right of return, so the seller must be able to see the buyer's till and the contract's real unit is the audit right; the seller now carries the buyer's market risk, the buyer's whole business becomes visible, and what fights it is a second till and every accounting that routes revenue around the counter; not a price set on the seller's own cost, which becomes invisible.

Quotient, not price: when the buyer's per-copy payment becomes one flat stream and the sellers stay many, the seller's unit becomes a share of a pool, as a streaming payout per play is the month's pot divided by the month's plays; the seller's price ceases to be a number anyone can set, and what becomes invisible is any way for one seller to charge more; not a low price but the absence of one, a residual that looks like a rate.

Reader becomes the ton: per copy becomes per thousand of the reader's attention sold to someone else, as a newspaper's price falls to zero and its unit becomes the impression, so the payer and the unit change places and neither buyer nor seller can count what is sold; a fourth party must host the meter, the ratings panel or the tracker, and what fights it is the reader who blocks the counter; not a discount to the reader, since the reader has stopped being the buyer.

Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software holding the buyer's files and music holding the buyer's playlists sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, and not film by subscription, where nothing accumulates and the margin is only the light viewer's absence, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.

Bought the forever: per event becomes per perpetuity, as a medieval donor stopped paying per mass and endowed a chantry to say them without end, so the unit is the seller's continued existence and the thing is pricable only if the seller is an institution that can outlive the buyer; the hostage flips sides, since the endowment holds the monastery to its masses, and what fights it is dissolution rather than churn; not a long subscription, since nothing is renewed and nobody can stop paying.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: milk assays, parcel cubes, tokens, beehives, demand charges, gyms, engine flight-hours, change orders, pest baselines, prizes, capitation, percentage rent, streaming pools, ratings panels, subscriptions, chantries; drawn from agriculture, freight, software, energy, medicine, construction, publishing, insurance, and one monastery.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases simplified to one mechanism each; Dead counter's meter-decay mechanism, Nearest countable's general law, and Cubed out's migration tendency are conjectural and marked so inside the items; no item is invented-world.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real contract usually carries several of these units at once (a two-part tariff is two of them), and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

The seriation is an itinerary of how far the priced unit has traveled from the thing handed over, not a ranking of sophistication, margin, or historical order; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (milk component pricing, engine flight-hour contracts, pollination rentals, chantries, per-mile insurance, streaming pools) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific contracts or their histories.

Dead counter's meter-decay mechanism, Nearest countable's claim that the unit moves toward the newest accepted meter, and Cubed out's migration toward the seller's binding constraint are conjectures held with visible modality; the near probe is built to test the first, none is asserted as established, and the map has no rule for which of the last two wins when they disagree.
Changes of price on an unchanged unit (levels, tiers, indexing, surge) and changes of the money (scrip, cigarettes) are outside; only a change in the kind of thing the buyer is buying is in.

seriation.axis: How far the priced unit has traveled from the thing handed over: from the thing itself measured more finely, through the seller's constraints and meters, across the ford of joint countability to the buyer's use, the buyer's outcomes and risk, the buyer's books, a third party's attention, and finally the seller's own continued existence.
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of sophistication or necessary stages. Assay eats the item opens it because the unit has not yet left the thing; Bought the forever closes it because the unit has become the seller. Meter in the seller's house → Nearest countable → Dead counter is the ford: the itinerary crosses from units on the seller's side to units on the buyer's side, it can cross only where a meter stands on the far bank, and the crossing is one-way wherever it leaves a meter behind. Sold your forecast of yourself → Thrust by the hour is the taught adjacency: both price the buyer's use of something the seller keeps, and they sit together on the walk, but the first lives on the buyer not seeing their utilization and the second exists to show it, so the neighbors on the line are the incompatibility on the map. Hostage shelf → Bought the forever is the closing hinge, where the hostage flips from buyer to seller. The last third of the walk, Losers pay the winner, Quotient, not price, and Hostage shelf, is ordered by the walk's hinges rather than by distance from the thing, as the independent critic noted; the itinerary admits it rather than claiming the axis reaches that far.

relations.to: Cubed out: the priced unit tends to migrate to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes, and the migration only completes where the constraint is something the buyer can measure too, a cube but not a queue; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price (a tendency observed in freight, not asserted as a law).
relations.label: If a buyer reserves capacity on the seller's binding constraint and that constraint moves, the reservation is on the wrong unit and reprices itself without anyone renegotiating; a lane reserved by weight becomes a windfall or a loss the day the trucks cube out before they weigh out.

exploration.first_question: When the unit that is priced changes kind, what does the new unit oblige: who now carries the measurement burden and the risk, what becomes visible or invisible, what fights it, and which of these changes can be undone?
exploration.changed_question: What must be true of the thing sold for a unit to be pricable at all, and who hosts the meter? The first breath assumed the two parties could count the new unit and were the only two parties. Sharpening Paternity test against pollination, an outcome nobody can count, showed the unit settling on the nearest jointly countable thing; following the meter from there produced units counted only by the seller, by a fourth party, or by nobody, a road back that closes when the old meter dies, and a seller whose price is a quotient.
exploration.new_member: Quotient, not price: when the buyer's per-copy payment becomes one flat stream and the sellers stay many, the seller's unit becomes a share of a pool, as a streaming payout per play is the month's pot divided by the month's plays; the seller's price ceases to be a number anyone can set, and what becomes invisible is any way for one seller to charge more; not a low price but the absence of one, a residual that looks like a rate.

priorities.item: Dead counter: per hour becomes per fixed bid, and the new unit is priced from the old one's records for exactly as long as they are kept, since nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on; a shop that dropped its timesheets when it went to fixed bids is estimating blind within a season, and cannot price a return to hourly estimates either, so the road back closes only behind a move that abandoned a meter, while per-year insurance, which needed no odometer, reopens at will; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.
priorities.why: It answers the live question about reversibility with a mechanism that can be checked cheaply, and if it holds it generalizes: every unit change is reversible exactly as long as somebody is paid to keep the old meter, which is a fact about accounting rather than about the thing sold.
priorities.next_question: Find ten shops that moved from hourly to fixed bid and ask whether they still keep timesheets; for each, ask what the first hourly bid after the switch cost them against its actual hours. If reversal is blocked by meter decay rather than by contract, the shops that kept timesheets went back cheaply and the others did not, and the size of the gap prices the dead meter.

priorities.item: Bought the forever: per event becomes per perpetuity, as a medieval donor stopped paying per mass and endowed a chantry to say them without end, so the unit is the seller's continued existence and the thing is pricable only if the seller is an institution that can outlive the buyer; the hostage flips sides, since the endowment holds the monastery to its masses, and what fights it is dissolution rather than churn; not a long subscription, since nothing is renewed and nobody can stop paying.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that most units have a perpetual form, high generative promise: it asks whether every unit can be capitalized into forever, and the ones that cannot show what the seller must be for the unit to exist at all.
priorities.next_question: Try to write an endowment for three units that have never been capitalized: per-token inference, per-mile insurance, a season pass. For each, find what the seller would have to be for the perpetuity to hold, and whether the unit fails because the seller is mortal, because the meter is, or because the thing sold is.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing five items (recasting Nearest countable and Dead counter as transformations that carry their laws as conjectural obligations, since the first was contradicted by three of the map's own one-sided meters and the second's case showed a different mechanism than it claimed; narrowing Hostage shelf's cases to ones with a hostage; correcting the token-count and freight-law modalities) and relabeling four edges whose musts and cannots had standing counterexamples, so the incompatibility and the one-way ford now hold as conditionals.

neighbors.left: Rent on the peak: per unit consumed becomes per unit of capacity held ready, as a factory pays a demand charge on its highest kilowatt rather than its kilowatt-hours, a shipper leases a dedicated lane, and a cloud tenant reserves instances that sit idle in its name; the buyer now carries utilization risk and the seller is paid to be idle on the buyer's behalf, the peak becomes visible and the average invisible; not an option that may be oversold, since the reservation must hold at the very moment everyone wants it.
neighbors.right: Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.
neighbors.separating_case: One coworking floor sold two ways. A dedicated desk is Rent on the peak: held empty in the tenant's name, the seller paid to keep it idle, and the reservation good on the day everyone shows up. A hot-desk membership on the same floor is Sold your forecast of yourself: more memberships than desks, the margin in the members who stay home, and on the day everyone shows up the unit fails. Same desk, same price, different unit: one is a promise that must hold at the peak, the other a bet that the peak never comes.

checks.boundary_case: Per hour becoming per day, or per unit becoming a volume tier, is out: the buyer still buys time or units, and nobody's measurement burden or risk moves, so a coarser or curved price on the same unit is a change of price, not of kind. Fence around done is in on exactly that contrast, since a fixed bid stops buying time at all.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence hides as adjacency: Paternity test → Paid for the nothing splits outcome pricing on the sign of the event, and the two branches need different instruments, an attribution rule for what occurred and a baseline for what did not. It shows an incompatibility between two itinerary neighbors, Sold your forecast of yourself and Thrust by the hour: both price the buyer's use of something the seller keeps, but the option unit lives on the buyer not seeing their utilization and the metered unit exists to show it, so one contract cannot carry both on the same use unless the metered rate is punitive, which is the telecom allowance plan's exception. It shows a passage between levels at Hostage shelf → Quotient, not price, where a change in the buyer's unit sends the variance between a flat inflow and a variable count somewhere, and where the platform refuses to hold it the seller's unit becomes a quotient and the seller's price disappears, and a second passage at Reader becomes the ton → Meter in the seller's house, where the meter leaves the seller's house for a fourth party's whenever the buyer will not accept the seller's own count. And it shows a broken loop at Nearest countable → Dead counter: the line reads as if a unit could walk back along the itinerary, and the edge says the ford is one-way exactly where the move leaves a meter behind to die.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not a self-read: the critic found the map's two most generative items were laws stated without transformations of their own and recast them as members of the type with their conjectures kept as obligations, relabeled four edges whose musts had standing counterexamples into conditionals, and admitted the map with its strange members (a price that is a quotient, a unit that is the seller's survival, a price paid by losers who never meet the buyer, a reader who becomes the ton) intact as mechanisms rather than softened into pricing advice.

name: cooperation-ignitions
of: A mechanism by which two parties with no shared history make a first cooperative move that the bare payoffs would forbid and that rests on neither party's word, whether or not a court stands behind the paper, named with its carrier, what makes the first move survivable, who can strike it (one side alone, both hands at once, a third with a stake, or nobody), and the residue it leaves that later limits the cooperation.
items: Twenty in the till: one party stages a windfall the other could keep without being caught, as a bar owner leaves a loose twenty in the drawer on a new bartender's first shift or a jeweler overpays a courier by one stone; the carrier is an apparent error, the first move is safe because the stake is small and its return is uncoerced information, and the residue is that the probe must stay secret forever, since a cooperation later found to have begun as a test reads as contempt; not a gift, which announces itself and makes a debt rather than a reading.

Gift already eaten: one party delivers something the other has consumed before it could decide whether to accept, as a produce broker drops a case of stone fruit at a restaurant's back door on a Friday or the drug company's lunch is on the table before the clinic is asked; the carrier is a good whose acceptance is performed by its arrival, the first move is safe because it is sized to what the giver can lose, and the residue is a debt in an unpriced currency that the giver may name later and the receiver can never fully close; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' recursive gift exchange, which is the running loop, and to cooperative-masks' favor unasked-for and priced later, which is this ignition used as a trap, this is the unrefusable first turn, which ignites whether or not the giver ever means to name the price, and its power is that no price was said.

Hostage before the ask: one party hands over, unrequested, something the other can destroy but not use, as a demolition subcontractor parks its excavator on the owner's lot the night before any contract is signed, or a touring band leaves its backline in the club's cellar before the settlement is agreed; the carrier is the hostage asymmetry Williamson called the ugly princess, precious to the giver and worth little to the holder, so that holding it tempts no one to provoke a default, the first move is safe because it costs nothing if the other cooperates and says what words cannot, and the residue is that the holder keeps a permanent option to destroy and the cooperation cannot grow past the hostage's value without a second hostage; not collateral demanded, which is a term, not source escrow or a bond, where a third party holds the thing and the counterpart gains its use on release, and not cooperation-mechanisms' retained hostages, which steady a cooperation already running; here the unasked giving is the whole signal.

First cut: one party destroys its own outside option in the other's sight, as a tailor cuts the bolt to the stranger's measurements before a deposit is paid or a machine shop tools a die for one customer's part; the carrier is a good made specific to one counterpart and so unsaleable to any other, the first move is safe because the cut is cheap against the job and the customer now knows the tailor cannot walk, and the residue is bilateral monopoly, since the customer can no longer get this coat elsewhere either, so the second negotiation is a hold-up; not a hostage, which is handed to someone, since after the cut nobody holds anything and the loss is simply made.

Lot you can lose: the good is cut to a piece small enough that losing it falls below the threshold of grievance, as a freight broker gives a new carrier one load, a restaurant orders one case, a magazine buys one story; the carrier is divisibility, the first move is safe because the worst case is a write-off and not a wound, and the residue is a ladder, since the cooperation can grow only one rung per successful lot and the trial price, set as a loss-leader, must rise later and reads as betrayal when it does; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sequential milestones, which need an agreed plan, this needs none, and what the lot proves is only the lot, which is why salted mines work.

Rule against myself: one party binds itself publicly to terms before any stranger arrives, as the Quaker shop posted one price and forswore haggling so a stranger could enter without fear of being fleeced, or a maintainer publishes under a license that cannot be revoked; the carrier is a rule addressed to no one in particular and visible in advance, the first move is safe because the surrendered upside of discretion is repaid by every stranger the rule lets in, and the residue is that the binder can no longer reward a friend, punish a cheat, or price a desperate buyer without breaking the rule that brought the strangers; at its far end lies a rule nobody wrote, the shipping container and the rail gauge, where the addressee is everyone not yet born and the cooperation is exactly as deep as the plug.

Summoned witness: one party makes its promise in front of people who will remember, as a shipbroker closes on the exchange floor by a word other brokers hear, a founder announces a partnership at the trade show before the paper is signed, a contributor's pledge sits in a public issue tracker; the carrier is an audience whose memory the promiser cannot edit, the first move is safe for the counterpart because breaking the promise now costs the promiser its other relationships, and the residue is that the promise freezes in the form the audience heard, so renegotiation looks like breach and the parties keep bad terms to avoid the look of it; unlike cooperation-mechanisms' reputation legible to future partners, which is stock accumulated over time, the witness is summoned at the first move and one side can summon it alone.

Beach with no faces: the exchange is arranged so that no step requires trusting the next, as in the reported silent trade where traders laid goods on the shore and withdrew, the other side laid gold beside them and withdrew, and the first party took the gold or left it if the pile was short; the carrier is a spatial protocol in which every move is retractable until the last, the first move is safe because at no moment does either party hold both goods, and the residue is that no channel exists, so the parties cannot complain, explain, bundle, or extend credit, and the cooperation cannot grow past spot exchange; Herodotus's account is disputed as history and is kept for the mechanism, which the atomic swap reproduces exactly, each side's transfer locked until the other's is revealed and either side free to walk until the last step; the escrowed darknet sale does not, since its market is a holder with a face, and a cash sale across a counter has the protocol without the residue, since the faces leave a channel and the beach's ceiling is bought by their absence, not by the protocol.

Price after the crop: neither party pays until the thing exists, so the price is a share of an output not yet made, as a landlord and a tenant with no history split the harvest, a lawyer takes a stranger's case for a third of the award, an author signs for a royalty; the carrier is the future output itself, the first move is safe because nothing changes hands now and each side risks only its own labor, and the residue is that every input is disputed, since each party bears the whole cost of what it adds and gets half the yield, so the yardstick becomes the second war; not the wager, which needs the parties to disagree, since this works when they agree and simply have no cash and no trust.

Wager that needs a partner: two parties who disagree about a fact write the disagreement as a contingent term each thinks favors it, as buyer and seller who cannot agree on a company's worth sign an earn-out, a landlord and a tenant who disagree about the traffic a corner will draw set the rent as a share of sales, two rivals bet on whose method yields more and must run the trial together; the carrier is a difference of belief, the first move is safe because each party expects to win, so the disagreement itself funds the cooperation, and the residue is that whoever measures wins, so the accounting or the trial design becomes the next fight; not impasse-inventions' graduated tie or contingent clause, which break a deadlock in a negotiation already running, since here there was no relationship and the disagreement is the fuel.

Sin in common: the first joint act is a transgression both commit, as two salespeople split a territory the company forbids them to split, two contractors on one site share a crew off the books, two prisoners hold one hidden phone; the carrier is a rule both break in the same act, the first move is safe because each becomes a witness against the other in the same instant, and the residue is that the cooperation can never be made public, expires with the secret's statute, and each partner keeps a knife; not mutual embarrassment discovered afterward, which is blackmail, and not the shared enemy, which stands outside the pair.

Promise that costs nothing yet: each party promises to pay in a state that has not occurred, as farmers in a county pledge to cover any barn that burns or shipowners pledge to share any hull lost; the carrier is a contingency improbable enough that the promise is nearly free to make, the first move is safe because nothing is paid until the loss and every other promiser is still exposed when it comes, and the residue is that the cooperation is untested until the first claim, which is the real ignition and arrives at the moment paying buys the payer nothing, since the claimant's good conduct is already spent and the payer's own barn still stands, and, when the shock is common and takes several hulls at once, arrives as well when the payer is poorest; not price after the crop, where the trigger is certain and only its size is unknown, and not cooperation-mechanisms' mutualization of risk, which is the pool running, since here the promise is the ignition and the first claim is its test.

Broker of both names: a third party with history on each side and no stake in the deal beyond its cut and its next introduction lends both its name, as a freight broker matches a shipper and a carrier who have never met, a literary agent puts a manuscript in an editor's hands, a Maghribi merchant vouched for an agent overseas; the carrier is a reputation held in the middle, the first move is safe because the broker loses its next match if either side cheats, and the residue is that the parties never build direct trust, the broker sees everything and takes a cut forever, and the first direct deal is the first betrayal; not an enforcer, since the broker can only withhold the next match, and not the bank's letter of credit, where nobody trusts anyone and each party transacts with the bank.

Peace of the fair: a bounded time and ground under a special rule suspends ordinary hostility so strangers can trade, as the medieval fair's peace, the Olympic truce, the Christmas truce of 1914, the trade show floor; the carrier is a calendar and a place, the first move is safe because the suspension is symmetrical and dated and everyone's ordinary state resumes at the bell, and the residue is that nothing done inside travels out, since the peace was the fair's and not the parties', though they leave with a date, the next fair, which is the first shadow of a future; the fair's own court and exclusion from the next fair are its only sanction, so it sits at the edge of the no-enforcer condition, and the truce in the trench had none at all.

Cargo that rots: one party arrives holding a good that decays faster than a negotiation can run, as a boat with a catch must sell to whoever is on the dock, a grower with fruit at the packing house, a printer with a press idle tonight; the carrier is the good's own clock, the first move is safe for the counterpart because the holder demonstrably cannot play a long game of holding out, and the residue is that the cooperation was priced at duress, the hurried party remembers a hold-up, and the next season opens with a grievance; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which is manufactured inside a negotiation, and one side can light this on purpose by choosing to arrive with something that will not keep.

Wall neither can lift: a shared exposure can be reduced only by joint action, as two rowhouse owners with one failing party wall, two farms behind one levee, two tenants over one blocked drain; the carrier is an indivisible physical liability, the first move is safe because contributing to the repair pays the mover in any case and only the other's share is at risk, and the residue is that the cooperation is coextensive with the wall and ends at the repair, so each party either hunts for the next wall or builds one to keep the partner; not the wall one owner can fix alone, which ignites nothing but a sucker, and not the shared enemy, which adapts.

Enemy at both doors: a third party whose harm falls on both makes defection between them costlier than cooperation, as two shipping lines form a conference against a third, two restaurants co-fund a street festival against the mall, two firms share one lawyer against a regulator; the carrier is an adversary that exploits any gap between the pair, the first move is safe because the enemy punishes non-cooperation more than the partner could, and the residue is that the cooperation is indexed to the enemy, has no floor when the enemy is gone, and each partner has taught the other how it fights; one side can counterfeit this by inventing the enemy, which cooperative-masks names as the manufactured shared enemy and impasse-inventions as the commissioned one, and what this item adds is the residue on each side of the counterfeit: an honest enemy leaves an alliance with no floor, and a staged one leaves the stager the probe's secret to keep and an enemy that must go on being fed.

Same cell: two parties are placed together with no exit by a third who did not consult them, as cellmates assigned, conscripts bunked, two firms condemned to share one pier, two shops the landlord assigned to one loading dock; the carrier is an imposed future in which the other cannot disappear, the first move is safe because the shadow of the future is already there without anyone's choosing it, and the residue is that the cooperation is an artifact of the cage and ends at release, since neither party ever chose the other and neither has learned whether it would; not the wall, which is a task, and not the enemy, which has a face; the cage is exit removed and nothing else.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: bar tills, source escrow, cut cloth, trial loads, sharecrops and contingency fees, posted prices and licenses, exchange floors, a silent shore, earn-outs, off-book crews, barn mutuals, freight brokers, fair peaces, fish docks, party walls, shipping conferences, cell assignments; drawn from restaurants, software, tailoring, freight, farming, law, publishing, insurance, retail, open source, medieval trade, and prisons.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the silent trade is a reported and disputed account kept for its mechanism; the sorting of ignitions by who can strike them, and the claim that a staged circumstance inherits the probe's residue, are the author's analytical inferences and are marked as such; no item is invented-world; 'a rule nobody wrote' in Rule against myself is a flourish, since the container standard had a committee, and the mechanism does not depend on it; 'reads as contempt' in Twenty in the till is the author's psychology, bounded where the probe is a trade's custom.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real first deal usually combines several ignitions (a lot, given as a gift, in front of a witness), and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.
The seriation is an itinerary of who can strike the match, not a ranking of strength, cost, or frequency; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (Quaker fixed prices, the fair peace, the 1914 truce, Maghribi agents, Herodotus's silent trade, county barn mutuals) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories; the silent trade in particular is disputed as history.

A court may stand behind the paper in many of these (the earn-out, the sharecrop, the license, the fair's own court); the map's condition, as the critic named it, is not that no enforcer exists but that the first move rests on neither stranger's word, and it excludes only cases where the contract itself is what makes the move safe, or where the parties never cooperate with each other at all, as under a letter of credit.

What keeps cooperation running once lit is outside the map (cooperation-mechanisms); the residues here name only the ceiling each ignition leaves behind, not its maintenance, and the claim that a staged circumstance inherits the probe's residue is the author's analytical inference, bounded where the probe is a trade's custom, since a discovered test then reads as routine and the secret residue shrinks toward nothing.

seriation.axis: Who can strike the match: from ignitions one party lights alone while the other does not even know a match was struck (a planted twenty), through ignitions one party lights and aims at a named counterpart (a gift, a hostage, a cut, a lot), to ignitions one party lights but addresses to no one (a posted rule, a summoned audience), to ignitions that need both hands at once (a shore, a share of a crop not yet grown, a wager, a sin, a pool of promises), to ignitions lit by a third with its own stake (a broker, a fair's host), and finally to ignitions nobody lights, which fall on both (a rotting cargo, a wall, an enemy, a cell).
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of strength or a sequence of stages. Twenty in the till opens it because only one hand is on the match and the other party never sees it; Same cell closes it because there is no hand at all, only a door someone else shut. Summoned witness → Beach with no faces is the hinge: the witness solves the untrustworthy first mover by adding as many eyes as possible, the beach by removing every face, and the crossing teaches that making breach expensive and making breach impossible are opposite cures for one disease, and that the beach pays for never needing an audience with the residue of never having a channel. Price after the crop was moved on the Fable critic's argument from the aimed group to the both-hands group beside the wager its discriminator is written against, since in a sharecrop, a contingency fee, or a royalty nothing is exposed until both have committed; the walk now reads Rule → Witness → Beach → Crop → Wager → Sin → Promise, and Beach → Crop teaches that removing the faces and deferring the price are two ways of having no first move. The far adjacency Enemy at both doors → Same cell teaches that the enemy is a cage with a face: remove the face and the cage remains, and the cooperation goes from being indexed to the enemy's presence to being indexed to the door's.

relations.from: Lot you can lose: the good is cut to a piece small enough that losing it falls below the threshold of grievance, as a freight broker gives a new carrier one load, a restaurant orders one case, a magazine buys one story; the carrier is divisibility, the first move is safe because the worst case is a write-off and not a wound, and the residue is a ladder, since the cooperation can grow only one rung per successful lot and the trial price, set as a loss-leader, must rise later and reads as betrayal when it does; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sequential milestones, which need an agreed plan, this needs none, and what the lot proves is only the lot, which is why salted mines work.
relations.to: Hostage before the ask: one party hands over, unrequested, something the other can destroy but not use, as a demolition subcontractor parks its excavator on the owner's lot the night before any contract is signed, or a touring band leaves its backline in the club's cellar before the settlement is agreed; the carrier is the hostage asymmetry Williamson called the ugly princess, precious to the giver and worth little to the holder, so that holding it tempts no one to provoke a default, the first move is safe because it costs nothing if the other cooperates and says what words cannot, and the residue is that the holder keeps a permanent option to destroy and the cooperation cannot grow past the hostage's value without a second hostage; not collateral demanded, which is a term, not source escrow or a bond, where a third party holds the thing and the counterpart gains its use on release, and not cooperation-mechanisms' retained hostages, which steady a cooperation already running; here the unasked giving is the whole signal.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanism do two parties with no shared history and no enforcer make a first cooperative move, what carries it, what makes that move survivable, and what does it leave behind that later limits the cooperation?
exploration.changed_question: Which ignitions work by shrinking the first move, and which by abolishing it, whether by making every step retractable, deferring the price until the thing exists, promising only in a state that has not occurred, addressing the rule to no one, or having exit removed by a third; and who can strike each, since the first breath's ignitions were all moves made toward a counterpart and exposed to it, and sharpening Lot you can lose against the silent trade showed that the strongest ignitions have no first move at all. The live question resolved into a finding: nearly every ignition that falls on both parties has a deliberate counterfeit one side can stage, and the counterfeit carries the probe's residue, since it must stay secret to keep working.
